the clause is a second adjective of كوكب. ﴿مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يوقد. ﴿مُبارَكَةٍ﴾: an adjective of شجرة. ﴿زَيْتُونَةٍ﴾: badal (substitute) for شجرة. ﴿لا﴾: redundant (zāʾida). ﴿شَرْقِيَّةٍ﴾: a second adjective of شجرة. ﴿وَلا غَرْبِيَّةٍ﴾: conjoined to what precedes. ﴿يَكادُ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb. ﴿زَيْتُها﴾: the noun of يكاد, and the hā is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يُضِيءُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the overt ḍamma, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar of يكاد. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); لو is a conditional particle that does not make the verb jussive. ﴿لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ﴾: لم is a particle making the verb jussive, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the hāʾ is its fronted object. ﴿نارٌ﴾: its postponed fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿نُورُ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلى نُورٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar; the clause emphasises what precedes it. ﴿يَهْدِي اللَّهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِنُورِهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يهدي, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَيَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿الْأَمْثالَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative. ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يضرب. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عليم. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾: khabar; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:36-38.t: ﴿فِي بُيُوتٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb. ﴿أَذِنَ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of بيوت. ﴿أَنْ تُرْفَعَ﴾: أن makes the verb accusative, and a passive imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿وَيُذْكَرَ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ترفع. ﴿فِيهَا﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يذكر. ﴿اسْمُهُ﴾: the nāʾib fāʿil of يذكر. ﴿يُسَبِّحُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿لَهُ فِيها﴾: prepositions and their genitive nouns, attached to يسبح. ﴿بِالْغُدُوِّ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is a second adjective of بيوت. ﴿وَالْآصالِ﴾: conjoined to الغدو. ﴿رِجالٌ﴾: the fāʿil of يسبح. ﴿لا تُلْهِيهِمْ﴾: لا is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿تِجارَةٌ﴾: postponed fāʿil; the clause is an adjective of رجال. ﴿وَلا بَيْعٌ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, لا is redundant (zāʾida), and بيع is conjoined to تجارة. ﴿عَنْ ذِكْرِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تلهيهم. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَإِقامِ﴾: conjoined to ذكر. ﴿الصَّلاةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَإِيتاءِ الزَّكاةِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes. ﴿يَخافُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿يَوْماً﴾: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to يخافون. ﴿تَتَقَلَّبُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative. ﴿فِيهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تتقلب. ﴿الْقُلُوبُ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿وَالْأَبْصارُ﴾: conjoined to القلوب. ﴿لِيَجْزِيَهُمُ﴾: the lām is the lām of reason (taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit أن after the lām of reason, and the hāʾ is a fronted first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿أَحْسَنَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ما﴾: a relative [noun], muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَيَزِيدَهُمْ﴾: conjoined to يجزيهم and parsed like it. ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يزيدهم. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). ﴿يَرْزُقُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative; the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْ﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يرزق. ﴿حِسابٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:39-40.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the relative noun is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿أَعْمالُهُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كَسَرابٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of الذين, and the clause of الذين with its khabar is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿بِقِيعَةٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective (ṣifa) of سراب. ﴿يَحْسَبُهُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its first object. ﴿الظَّمْآنُ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿ماءً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a second adjective of سراب. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and of the genitive. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) containing the sense of condition. ﴿جاءَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, its fāʿil being a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَمْ يَجِدْهُ﴾: لم is a particle making the verb jussive, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm); the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi and its fāʿil is latent; the clause has no position because it is the answer of a condition that does not make the verb jussive. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَوَجَدَ اللَّهَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its object, its fāʿil being latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿عِنْدَهُ﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to وجد, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَوَفَّاهُ حِسابَهُ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its object, its fāʿil being latent; حسابه is its second object, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَاللَّهُ سَرِيعُ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and mubtadaʾ and khabar. ﴿الْحِسابِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿كَظُلُماتٍ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to كسراب. ﴿فِي بَحْرٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of ظلمات. ﴿لُجِّيٍّ﴾: an adjective of بحر. ﴿يَغْشاهُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fronted object. ﴿مَوْجٌ﴾: postponed fāʿil; the clause is a second adjective of بحر. ﴿مِنْ فَوْقِهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مَوْجٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is an adjective of موج. ﴿مِنْ فَوْقِهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿سَحابٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the adjective of the second موج. ﴿ظُلُماتٌ﴾: khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya). ﴿بَعْضُها﴾: mubtadaʾ, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَوْقَ﴾: an adverb of place, attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿بَعْضٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is an adjective of ظلمات. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb containing the sense of condition, attached to its answer. ﴿أَخْرَجَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿يَدَهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَمْ يَكَدْ﴾: لم makes the verb jussive, and an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive by لم, whose noun is omitted. [Translator's note: so in the source; the noun of يكد is usually taken as a latent pronoun.] ﴿يَراها﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of يكد. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; من is a conditional [noun] making the verb jussive, mubtadaʾ, and its clause is resumptive. ﴿لَمْ يَجْعَلِ اللَّهُ﴾: لم makes the verb jussive, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿لَهُ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يجعل. ﴿نُوراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَما﴾: the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ما is negating; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the condition. ﴿لَهُ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ نُورٍ﴾: من is redundant (zāʾida); نور is mubtadaʾ, genitive (majrūr) in form and nominative (marfūʿ) in position. The clauses of the condition and the answer are the khabar of من.

daas-irab:41-42.t: ﴿أَلَمْ﴾: the hamza is interrogative; لم is a particle making the verb jussive. ﴿تَرَ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter, whose fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: أنّ, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; أنّ and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of تر. ﴿يُسَبِّحُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿لَهُ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يسبح. ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السموات. ﴿وَالطَّيْرُ﴾: conjoined to من. ﴿صَافَّاتٍ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿كُلٌّ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). ﴿قَدْ﴾: a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿عَلِمَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿صَلاتَهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَتَسْبِيحَهُ﴾: conjoined to صلاته, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِما﴾: ما is a relative [noun]; [the two are] attached to عليم. ﴿يَفْعَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلِلَّهِ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and a preposition and the Name of Majesty, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مُلْكُ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾: conjoined to السموات. ﴿وَإِلَى اللَّهِ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿الْمَصِيرُ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes.

daas-irab:43-43.t: ﴿أَلَمْ﴾: the hamza is interrogative, and لم makes the verb jussive. ﴿تَرَ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: أنّ and its noun; it stands in place of the two objects of تر. ﴿يُزْجِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أنّ. ﴿سَحاباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿يُؤَلِّفُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿بَيْنَهُ﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) يؤلف, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿يَجْعَلُهُ رُكاماً﴾: an imperfect verb and its first object, its fāʿil being latent, and ركاما is its second object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَتَرَى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the alif because [its pronunciation] is impossible, and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿الْوَدْقَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi; it is the rain. ﴿يَخْرُجُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿مِنْ خِلالِهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يخرج. ﴿وَيُنَزِّلُ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يخرج and parsed like it. [Translator's note: so in the source; in sense ينزل is conjoined to يزجي, whose agent is Allah.] ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ينزل. ﴿مِنْ﴾: a redundant (zāʾid) preposition. ﴿جِبالٍ﴾: genitive (majrūr) in form, accusative (manṣūb) in position, as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِيها﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ﴾: a redundant preposition. ﴿بَرَدٍ﴾: genitive in form, nominative in position, as postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of جبال. ﴿فَيُصِيبُ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يصيب. ﴿مِنْ﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَيَصْرِفُهُ﴾: conjoined to فيصيب. ﴿عَنْ مَنْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يصرف. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَكادُ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb. ﴿سَنا﴾: the noun of يكاد, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the alif because [its pronunciation] is impossible; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿بَرْقِهِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَذْهَبُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِالْأَبْصارِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the khabar of يكاد.

daas-irab:44-46.t: ﴿يُقَلِّبُ اللَّهُ اللَّيْلَ﴾: an imperfect verb, the Name of Majesty its fāʿil (agent) and الليل its object; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿وَالنَّهارَ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿إِنَّ﴾ [Translator's note: no analysis is given for this word in the source; it is إنّ, the particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters).] ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of genitive, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate); the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿لَعِبْرَةً﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and عبرة is the noun of إنّ. ﴿لِأُولِي﴾: أولي is genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is treated like (mulḥaq bi-) the sound masculine plural; [the two are] attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of عبرة. ﴿الْأَبْصارِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿خَلَقَ كُلَّ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil being a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is the khabar. ﴿دَابَّةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ ماءٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خلق. ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition), and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ﴾: a relative [noun], mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَمْشِي﴾: an imperfect verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلى بَطْنِهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يمشي, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى رِجْلَيْنِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى أَرْبَعٍ﴾: conjoined to what precedes. ﴿يَخْلُقُ اللَّهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, with the Name of Majesty as its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾: a relative [noun], mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَشاءُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾: إنّ, the Name of Majesty its noun and قدير its khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قدير, and شيء is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَقَدْ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿أَنْزَلْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause answering the oath has no position. ﴿آياتٍ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿مُبَيِّناتٍ﴾: an adjective of آيات, accusative. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness, and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is omitted; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿إِلى صِراطٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يهدي. ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾: an adjective.

daas-irab:47-48.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿آمَنَّا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, and [the two are] attached to (mutaʿalliq) آمنا. ﴿وَبِالرَّسُولِ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَطَعْنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to آمنا. ﴿ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّى﴾: a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif because [its pronunciation] is impossible. ﴿فَرِيقٌ﴾: fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of فريق. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يتولى. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما operates like ليس. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: the demonstrative is in the position of nominative as its noun, and the kāf is for address. ﴿بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and a noun genitive in form, accusative (manṣūb) in position, with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; it is the khabar (predicate) of ما. ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) containing the sense of condition, putting its protasis in the genitive [by annexation] and made accusative by its answer. ﴿دُعُوا﴾: a passive past verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, genitive by إلى; the two are attached to دعوا. ﴿والرسول﴾: conjoined to الله. ﴿لِيَحْكُمَ﴾: the lām is the lām of reason (taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit أن after the lām of reason, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; أن and what follows it, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), [with the preposition] are attached to دعوا. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to يحكم, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِذا﴾: [إذا] of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya). ﴿فَرِيقٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of فريق. ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾: khabar, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural.

daas-irab:49-51.t: ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional. ﴿يَكُنْ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لَهُمُ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾: the noun of يكن, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿يَأْتُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يأتوا. ﴿مُذْعِنِينَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a masculine plural; the clause is the apodosis of a condition not joined with the fāʾ, with no position. ﴿أَفِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾: the hamza is interrogative, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مَرَضٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿أَمِ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿ارْتابُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿أَمِ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿يَخافُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَنْ﴾: [a particle] making the verb accusative. ﴿يَحِيفَ اللَّهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative by أن, and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يحيف. ﴿وَرَسُولُهُ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty. ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ, and the kāf is for address. ﴿هُمُ﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الظَّالِمُونَ﴾: khabar, nominative with the wāw; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّما﴾: the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿كانَ قَوْلَ﴾: كان (of kāna and its sisters) and its fronted khabar. ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) containing the sense of condition. ﴿دُعُوا﴾: a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, genitive by إلى; the two are attached to دعوا. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿أَنْ يَقُولُوا﴾: أن makes the verb accusative, and an imperfect verb, accusative by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; أن and what follows it are to be interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) in the position of nominative as the noun of كان. ﴿سَمِعْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَأَطَعْنا﴾: conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾: its i'rab has preceded in verse 50.

daas-irab:52-53.t: ﴿وَمَنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; من is a conditional [noun] making the verb jussive, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿يُطِعِ اللَّهَ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its object being the Name of Majesty, and its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَيَخْشَ اللَّهَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the Name of Majesty is its object and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿وَيَتَّقْهِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it, jussive like it. ﴿فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفائِزُونَ﴾: its i'rab is like that of أولئك هم المفلحون or الظالمون. ﴿وَأَقْسَمُوا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أقسموا. ﴿جَهْدَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَيْمانِهِمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَئِنْ﴾: the lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), and إن is conditional. ﴿أَمَرْتَهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لَيَخْرُجُنَّ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the omitted oath, and an imperfect verb from which the wāw of the plural has been dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns; the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the nūn of the nominative has been dropped because of the succession of like [letters]; the clause has no position because it is the answer to an oath. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لا تُقْسِمُوا﴾: لا is prohibitive, and an imperfect verb, jussive by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿طاعَةٌ﴾: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي طاعة". ﴿مَعْرُوفَةٌ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ﴾: إنّ, its noun and its khabar; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), with no position. ﴿بِما﴾: ما is a relative [noun]; [the two are] attached to the khabar. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative.

daas-irab:54-55.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ﴾: an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and the Name of Majesty is its object; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction and إن is conditional. ﴿تَوَلَّوْا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿فَإِنَّما﴾: the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and إنما is the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿ما﴾: a relative [noun], postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the condition. ﴿حُمِّلَ﴾: a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَلَيْكُمْ ما﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿حُمِّلْتُمْ﴾: a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional. ﴿تُطِيعُوهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive by the dropping of the nūn; it is the protasis; the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the clause is initial, with no position. ﴿تَهْتَدُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive by the dropping of the nūn; it is the apodosis, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a condition not joined with the fāʾ. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is resumptive and ما is negating. ﴿عَلَى الرَّسُولِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿الْبَلاغُ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْمُبِينُ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ﴾: a past verb, the Name of Majesty its fāʿil and the relative noun its object. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to آمنوا. ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the hāʾ is its object and its fāʿil is latent; the clause has no position because it is the answer to an oath. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the preceding verb. ﴿كَمَا﴾: the kāf is a preposition and ما is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). ﴿اسْتَخْلَفَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi; أن and what follows it are to be interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) in the position of genitive by the kāf, and [the two are] attached to an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). [Translator's note: the source says «أن», but the particle here is the maṣdariyya ما.] ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ﴾: conjoined to ليستخلفنهم and parsed like it. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يمكنن. ﴿دِينَهُمُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, adjective of دين. ﴿ارْتَضى﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif because [its pronunciation] is impossible, and its fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ارتضى. ﴿وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ﴾: conjoined to ليمكنن and parsed like it; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the preceding verb. ﴿خَوْفِهِمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَمْناً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَعْبُدُونَنِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the yāʾ its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is resumptive and لا is negating. ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِي﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يشركون. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; من is a conditional [noun], mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَفَرَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بَعْدِ﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to كفر. [Translator's note: so in the source; بعد here is an adverb of time.] ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of genitive; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾: the fāʾ connects the apodosis, and أولاء, the demonstrative, is mubtadaʾ; the kāf is for address. ﴿هُمُ﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْفاسِقُونَ﴾: the khabar of أولئك; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the condition.

daas-irab:56-58.t:
﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent) and الصلاة its object; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it and parsed like it. ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا﴾: conjoined to what precedes it and parsed like it. ﴿الرَّسُولَ﴾: conjoined to the earlier وأطيعوا الله. [Translator's note: so in the source; الرسول is the object of أطيعوا, and the clause as a whole recalls وأطيعوا الله in verse 54.] ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾: لعلّ and its noun; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), with no position. ﴿تُرْحَمُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿لا تَحْسَبَنَّ﴾: لا is prohibitive, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مُعْجِزِينَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi of تحسبن. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَمَأْواهُمُ النَّارُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَلَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath, and an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame, and المصير is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: parsed previously.
﴿لِيَسْتَأْذِنْكُمُ﴾: the lām is the lām of command, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command, and the kāf is its object. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as fāʿil. ﴿مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: conjoined to the preceding الذين. ﴿لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا﴾: لم makes the verb jussive, and an imperfect verb, jussive by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿الْحُلُمَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿ثَلاثَ﴾: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to يستأذنكم. ﴿مَرَّاتٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي من قبل". ﴿صَلاةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْفَجْرِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَحِينَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an adverb of time. ﴿تَضَعُونَ ثِيابَكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; ثيابكم is mafʿūl bihi and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنَ الظَّهِيرَةِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تضعون. ﴿وَمِنْ بَعْدِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿صَلاةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْعِشاءِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ثَلاثَ﴾: khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي ثلاث". ﴿عَوْراتٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of عورات. ﴿لَيْسَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; the clause is resumptive. ﴿جُناحٌ﴾: the noun of ليس. ﴿بَعْدَهُنَّ﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to جناح, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: so in the source; بعد here is an adverb of time.] ﴿طَوَّافُونَ﴾: khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم طوافون". ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to طوافون; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾: the kāf is a preposition and ذا is a demonstrative; [the two are] attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يبين. ﴿الْآياتِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its two khabars; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:59-60.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) containing the sense of condition. ﴿بَلَغَ الْأَطْفالُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنْكُمُ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الْحُلُمَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَلْيَسْتَأْذِنُوا﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the answer of إذا, the lām is the lām of command, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause has no position because it is the answer of a condition that does not make the verb jussive. ﴿كَمَا﴾: the kāf is a preposition; ما is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). ﴿اسْتَأْذَنَ الَّذِينَ﴾: a past verb, and the relative noun is the fāʿil; ما and what follows it are to be interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) in the position of genitive by the kāf; [the two are] attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, with the Name of Majesty as its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يبين. ﴿آياتِهِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its two khabars (predicates); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَالْقَواعِدُ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنَ النِّساءِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿اللَّاتِي﴾: a relative noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as an adjective (ṣifa) of القواعد. ﴿لا يَرْجُونَ﴾: لا is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿نِكاحاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَلَيْسَ﴾: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿جُناحٌ﴾: the noun of ليس; the clause is the khabar of القواعد. ﴿أَنْ يَضَعْنَ﴾: أن makes the verb accusative, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural, and the nūn is the fāʿil. ﴿ثِيابَهُنَّ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿غَيْرَ﴾: ḥāl. ﴿مُتَبَرِّجاتٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِزِينَةٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to متبرجات. ﴿وَأَنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive and أن makes the verb accusative. ﴿يَسْتَعْفِفْنَ﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural, and the nūn is the fāʿil; أن and what follows it are to be interpreted as a maṣdar, [which is] mubtadaʾ. ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾: khabar. ﴿لَهُنَّ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خير. ﴿وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾: the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ, and سميع and عليم are its two khabars; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:61-61.t: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَى الْأَعْمى حَرَجٌ﴾: ليس is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb and حرج is its noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the fronted khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negating. ﴿عَلَى الْأَعْرَجِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿حَرَجٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَلا عَلَى الْمَرِيضِ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا عَلى أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿أَنْ تَأْكُلُوا﴾: أن makes the verb accusative, and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); أن and what follows it are to be interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar), [which is] mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تأكلوا, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَوْ بُيُوتِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿آبائِكُمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَوْ بُيُوتِ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ إِخْوانِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَخَواتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَعْمامِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ عَمَّاتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَخْوالِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ خالاتِكُمْ﴾: conjoined to what precedes. ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, conjoined to what precedes. ﴿مَلَكْتُمْ مَفاتِحَهُ﴾: a past verb; the tāʾ is its fāʿil, مفاتحه its object, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿أَوْ صَدِيقِكُمْ﴾: conjoined to what precedes. ﴿لَيْسَ﴾: an incomplete past verb. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿جُناحٌ﴾: the postponed noun of ليس; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنْ تَأْكُلُوا﴾: أن makes the verb accusative, and an imperfect verb, accusative by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَوْ أَشْتاتاً﴾: conjoined to جميعا. ﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) containing the sense of condition; the statement is resumptive. ﴿دَخَلْتُمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بُيُوتاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَسَلِّمُوا﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the answer of إذا, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause has no position because it is the answer of a condition that does not make the verb jussive. ﴿عَلى أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to سلموا, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿تَحِيَّةً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of تحية. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿طَيِّبَةً﴾: a second adjective of تحية. ﴿مُبارَكَةً﴾: also an adjective. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾: the kāf is a preposition and the demonstrative is in the position of genitive; [the two are] attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, with the Name of Majesty as its fāʿil. ﴿لَكُمُ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يبين. ﴿الْآياتِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾: لعلّ is a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters), and the kāf is its noun; the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), with no position. ﴿تَعْقِلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of لعلّ.

daas-irab:62-62.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا﴾: the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative [noun], khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ; the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) آمنوا. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an adverb (ẓarf) containing the sense of condition. ﴿كانُوا﴾: كان (of kāna and its sisters) and its noun; the clause is the ṣila. [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere the clause after إذا is parsed as muḍāf ilayhi.] ﴿مَعَهُ﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿عَلى أَمْرٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿جامِعٍ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of أمر. ﴿لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا﴾: لم makes the verb jussive, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause has no position because it is the answer of a condition that does not make the verb jussive. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and of the genitive. ﴿يَسْتَأْذِنُوهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit أن after حتى; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أن and what follows it, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), [with the preposition] are attached to يذهبوا. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾: إنّ, and the relative noun is its noun. ﴿يَسْتَأْذِنُونَكَ﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the khabar. [Translator's note: so in the source; the clause is the ṣila of الذين.] ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ, and the kāf is for address. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, khabar; the clause is the khabar of إنّ. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يؤمنون. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾: conjoined. ﴿فَإِذَا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and an adverb containing the sense of condition; the statement is resumptive. ﴿اسْتَأْذَنُوكَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the ṣila. [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere the clause after إذا is parsed as muḍāf ilayhi.] ﴿لِبَعْضِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يستأذنوك. ﴿شَأْنِهِمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَأْذَنْ﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the answer of إذا, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause has no position. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾: من is a relative [noun], and [the two are] attached to the verb. ﴿شِئْتَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to شئت. ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿لَهُمُ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾: the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾: إنّ, its noun and its two khabars; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), with no position.

daas-irab:63-64.t: ﴿لا﴾: prohibitive. ﴿تَجْعَلُوا دُعاءَ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and ﴿دُعاءَ﴾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿الرَّسُولِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كَدُعاءِ﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), second mafʿūl bihi, and دعاء is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَعْضِكُمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَعْضاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi of دعاء. ﴿قَدْ﴾: a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, with the Name of Majesty as its fāʿil. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَتَسَلَّلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it. ﴿لِواذاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَلْيَحْذَرِ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition), the lām is the lām of command, and an imperfect verb, jussive. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, fāʿil; the clause has no position. ﴿يُخالِفُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿عَنْ أَمْرِهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before it; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَنْ تُصِيبَهُمْ فِتْنَةٌ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb); the hāʾ is its object and فتنة its postponed fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَوْ يُصِيبَهُمْ عَذابٌ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it and parsed like it. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿أَلا﴾: an opening particle (adāt istiftāḥ). ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr) by the lām; [the two are] attached to the fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿ما﴾: a relative [noun], the noun of إنّ. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila of the relative. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾: conjoined. ﴿قَدْ﴾: a particle of verification. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿ما﴾: a relative [noun], mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يُرْجَعُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَيُنَبِّئُهُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِما﴾: ما is a relative [noun]; [the two are] attached to ينبئهم. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عليم. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾: khabar; the clause is resumptive.

dervis-irab:11-11.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الإفك): the most extreme form of lying; it is also said to be a slander (buhtān) of which you are unaware until it takes you by surprise. Its root is al-ifk, which is "turning over", because it is speech turned away (maʾfūk) from its proper face.
(كِبْرَهُ): the kibr of a thing, with kasra on the kāf and sukūn on the bāʾ, is its greater part. Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm said, mentioning a woman:
تنام عن كبر شأنها فاذا ... قامت رويدا تكاد تنغرف
(She sleeps through the greater part of her affairs, and when she rises, slowly, she almost bends and breaks.)
[Translator's note: the source prints the poet's name as «فيس», an evident misprint for «قيس» (Qays).]

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جاؤُ بِالْإِفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِنْكُمْ): the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), beginning the narration of the story of the slander (al-ifk). It runs over eighteen verses that will follow in sequence, and it concerns ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her; she was a righteous woman deserving of praise and commendation, so whoever accused her of evil has, as it were, overturned and obliterated the facts. إنّ and its noun; the clause جاءوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; بالإفك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) جاءوا; عصبة is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; منكم is a naʿt (adjective) of عصبة, i.e. from among the believers, even if only outwardly — for ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, one of those who plunged into the talk of the slander, was among the chief hypocrites. The clause لا تحسبوه is resumptive; the address here is to the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿĀʾisha and Ṣafwān, as consolation for them. The story of the slander will come in the section on benefits.
(لا تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرًّا لَكُمْ بَلْ هُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ): لا is jussive-governing; تحسبوه is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm); the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); شرا is the second direct object; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شرّ; بل is a conjunction indicating digression (iḍrāb); هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and خير the khabar; لكم is attached to خير. The aspect of good in it is the reward that the one afflicted by the trial obtains, then the manifestation of honour and the shining clarity of the truth through the revelation of eighteen verses declaring your innocence, and the dire threat of punishment against whoever plunged into it with evil intent and purpose.
(لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ مَا اكْتَسَبَ مِنَ الْإِثْمِ): لكل امرئ is a fronted khabar; منهم is a naʿt of امرئ; ما is a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause اكتسب is its ṣila; من الإثم is attached to اكتسب.
(وَالَّذِي تَوَلَّى كِبْرَهُ مِنْهُمْ لَهُ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; الذي is a mubtadaʾ; the clause تولى كبره is the ṣila, i.e. he went to extremes in it, magnified matters and embellished them out of the evil of his inner self and the wickedness of his heart; منهم is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). He is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, the hypocrite. له is a fronted khabar and عذاب عظيم a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of الذي.

* Benefits:
The account of the slander (ḥadīth al-ifk):
It is reported in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, in the words of ʿĀʾisha, who said: "I was with the Prophet ﷺ on an expedition after the ḥijāb had been revealed. He finished it and returned, and drew near to Medina, and one night he gave the order to set off. I walked away, attended to my need, and came back towards the camel saddle, and behold, my necklace had broken. So I went back to look for it, and they lifted my howdah thinking I was in it — the women were light then; they ate only a small amount (al-ʿulqa) of food. I found my necklace and came after they had moved off, so I sat down in the halting place where I had been, thinking the people would miss me and come back for me. My eyes overcame me and I slept. Ṣafwān had stopped for rest (ʿarrasa) behind the army, then set off early in the night (adlaja) after resting, travelled from there, and reached my halting place in the morning. He saw the dark shape of a sleeping person and recognised me when he saw me, for he used to see me before the ḥijāb. I woke up at his saying 'We belong to Allah and to Him we return' (istirjāʿ) when he recognised me, and I covered my face. By Allah, he did not speak a single word to me, nor did I hear any word from him other than his istirjāʿ, when he made his mount kneel and stepped on its foreleg. Then he set off leading the mount with me on it until we reached the army after they had halted, entering the fierce heat (mūghirīn) at high noon. Then those who perished on my account perished, and the one who took the greater part of it upon himself among them was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl."
Explanation of the rare words of the ḥadīth:
1- His words "on an expedition": it is said to be the expedition of al-Muraysīʿ, also called the expedition of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq. It took place in the fourth year, or it is said in the sixth. Its cause was that news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that Banū al-Muṣṭaliq were gathering to fight him, their leader being al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Ḍirār, the father of Juwayriya, wife of the Prophet ﷺ. When he heard of this he went out against them until he met them at one of their watering places called al-Muraysīʿ, in the direction of Qudayd towards the coast. They fought, and Allah routed Banū al-Muṣṭaliq and gave His Messenger power over their children, women and wealth, which he took as spoil (afāʾahā) and then returned to them.
2- "They ate al-ʿulqa": with ḍamma on the ʿayn and sukūn on the lām, a small amount of food.
3- Ṣafwān: he is the eminent Companion Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal al-Sulamī.
4- ʿArrasa: with shadda and fatḥa on the rāʾ, i.e. he halted by night to rest; it is specific to the last part of the night.
5- Adlaja: with shadda and fatḥa on the dāl, he travelled from the beginning of the night.
6- "At his istirjāʿ": i.e. at his saying "We belong to Allah and to Him we return."
7- "I covered my face with my jilbāb": i.e. I covered it with the wrap (al-mulāʾa).
8- "And stepped on its foreleg": i.e. he put his foot on its knee.
9- Mūghirīn: in al-Qāmūs: al-waghra is intense heat; waghrat al-hājira (on the pattern of waʿada) [the midday heat became intense], and awgharū means they entered into it. Al-waghr, also with a vowelled ghayn: rancour, malice, enmity and blazing with rage; waghira ṣadruhu (on the patterns of waʿada and wajila), waghran and wagharan with vowelling. And in al-Miṣbāḥ: "And he fell into a desert land, he came to be in it."
The Orientalists' version: The account of the slander has occupied the Orientalists, who have cast it in various versions. We present here, for information, the version of Brockelmann, the German Orientalist, author of the book "History of the Islamic Peoples". The following is the text of its Arabic translation:
"During the year 627 the Prophet also undertook several campaigns against some of the Bedouin tribes, and in one of them he went so far as to come near Mecca. These raids were safe to an extent that allowed him to take two of his wives along. It happened once that his favourite wife ʿĀʾisha bint Abī Bakr — who was then fourteen years old — lost her necklace, so she went out in the evening to look for it, and the caravans of the raiders left without her. She did not return to the camp until the following day, accompanied by a young man whom she had known before. Doubt about ʿĀʾisha's faithfulness crept into the Prophet's soul, so he sent her back to her parents' house. But Allah soon declared her innocent, after a single month, in one of the verses revealed to the Prophet, adding at the same time that any accusation of a woman of marital infidelity not supported by four eyewitnesses is considered a calumny or slander (qadhf) for which its author deserves a hundred lashes. ʿAlī, the Prophet's son-in-law, was one of ʿĀʾisha's adversaries who urged him to divorce her, and there is no doubt that the roots of the hostility ʿĀʾisha revealed towards ʿAlī after he became caliph over the Muslims go back to this period. Be that as it may, this incident of the necklace did not have the slightest effect on the social status of women in Islam, as is supposed: the veil adopted by married women was an ancient Arab custom, and the Prophet had imposed it before this incident for other reasons. In fact the veil did not prevent women in the Jāhiliyya, and in Islam too until the Umayyad era, from appearing among people with much freedom and from influencing Arab society, at times notably. The institution of the harem, whose rules the Abbasids laid down on the model of the Christian-Byzantine pattern, is alone responsible for the decline of women in the East."
Brockelmann's version, for all its precision, is not free of flaws, errors and a hidden prejudice which its author tries to conceal but which insists on showing itself; among this is his saying "so he sent her back to her parents' house".
[Translator's note: the source prints «ففاتتها فوافل الغزاة», evidently a misprint for «قوافل» (caravans); translated accordingly.]
The return to Medina and the clamour of talk:
Let us return to ʿĀʾisha's own account in the remainder of the aforementioned ḥadīth. She said:
"When we arrived in Medina I fell ill for a month, while the people were busily spreading what the people of the slander said, and I was unaware of any of it. What made me uneasy in my illness was that I did not see from the Messenger of Allah the kindness I used to see from him when I was ill; the Messenger of Allah would only come in, greet, and then say: 'How is that one of yours (tīkum)?' That made me uneasy, but I was not aware of the evil until I went out after I had convalesced, and Umm Misṭaḥ went out with me towards al-Manāṣiʿ. Then we came back, and Umm Misṭaḥ stumbled over her wrap and said: 'May Misṭaḥ perish!'
I said: 'What an evil thing you have said! Do you revile a man who was present at Badr?'
She said: 'O you (hantāh), have you not heard what he said?'
I said: 'And what did he say?'
So she told me what the people of the slander said, and my illness increased upon my illness. When I returned to my house I asked permission to go to my parents, wanting to make sure of the news from them, and he gave me permission.
My mother said: 'Take it easy, for by Allah, seldom has there been a beautiful woman with a man who loves her and who has co-wives, but that they have said much against her.'
I said: 'Glory be to Allah! Have people really been talking about this?' I wept that night until morning; my tears did not cease and I could not get any sleep.
The Messenger of Allah called ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Usāma ibn Zayd, consulting them about parting from his wife. As for Usāma ibn Zayd, he advised the Messenger of Allah according to what he knew of the innocence of his family and of the love he felt in himself for them, and said to the Messenger of Allah: 'They are your family, and we know nothing but good.'
As for ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: 'Allah has not constrained you, and there are many women besides her; and if you ask the maidservant she will tell you the truth.'
So the Messenger of Allah called Barīra and asked her: 'Have you seen anything from ʿĀʾisha that makes you suspicious?' She said: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, I have never seen anything in her that I could fault her with, more than that she is a young girl who falls asleep beside her family's dough, and the domestic goat comes and eats it.'
.. I wept that day of mine; my tears did not cease and I could not get any sleep. Then I wept the following night; my tears did not cease and I could not get any sleep, and my parents thought that the weeping would split my liver.
While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah came in, greeted, then sat down, recited the testimony of faith, and then said: 'To proceed, O ʿĀʾisha: such-and-such has reached me about you. If you are innocent, Allah will declare your innocence; and if you have committed a sin, then seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses a sin and then repents, Allah turns to him in forgiveness.'
When the Messenger of Allah had finished his words, my tears dried up until I could not feel a single drop of them. I said to my father: 'Answer the Messenger of Allah for me.' He said: 'By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah.' So I said to my mother: 'Answer for me.' She said: 'Likewise, by Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah.' I said — and I was a young girl who did not recite much of the Qur'an —:
'By Allah, I know that you have heard this until it has settled in your souls and you have believed it. If I tell you that I am innocent, you will not believe me; and if I confess something to you — and Allah knows that I am innocent — you would believe me. By Allah, I find no example for me and you except as the father of Yūsuf said: «فصبر جميل والله المستعان على ما تصفون» (so patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe).'
Then I turned over and lay down on my bed. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah had not left his seat, nor had anyone of the household gone out, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down revelation upon His Prophet, and there seized him what used to seize him of intense distress (al-buraḥāʾ) at revelation, so that drops of sweat like pearls would roll down from him on a winter day.
When it was lifted from the Messenger of Allah, and he was laughing, the first word he spoke was to say: 'Rejoice, O ʿĀʾisha! As for Allah, He has declared you innocent.'
My mother said to me: 'Get up and go to him.'
I said: 'By Allah, I will not get up to go to him, and I will praise none but Allah, who sent down my innocence.'
Abū Bakr used to spend on Misṭaḥ because of his kinship with him and his poverty, and he swore never to spend anything on him again. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: «ولا يأتل أولو الفضل منكم والسعة أن يؤتوا أولي القربى ... إلى قوله: ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم» (And let not those of virtue and means among you swear not to give to relatives … up to His words: Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?)
Abū Bakr said: 'By Allah, I do love that Allah should forgive me,' and he restored to Misṭaḥ the maintenance he used to spend on him."
What relates to this ḥadīth will come in the remaining verses.
[Translator's note: the source text reads «كما قال أبو يوسف» ("as Abū Yūsuf said"), i.e. the father of Yūsuf (Jacob); rendered "the father of Yūsuf". It also reads «فنأكله» ("and we eat it") in Barīra's words, evidently for «فتأكله» ("and it eats it"); translated as the latter.]

dervis-irab:12-15.t:
* I'rab:
(لَوْلا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتُ بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ خَيْراً): resumptive (mustaʾnaf) speech, beginning the rebuke of those who plunged into the slander and reproaching them for the rumours they spread. Nine successive rebukes will follow, and this is the first rebuke. لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) containing the sense of rebuke and reproach, which is frequent in the language when it enters upon a verb, as in His words, Exalted is He, «لولا أخرتني». إذ is an adverb of past time attached to (mutaʿalliq) ظنّ; the clause سمعتموه is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it. ظن المؤمنون is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); والمؤمنات is conjoined (maʿṭūf); بأنفسهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خيرا; خيرا is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(وَقالُوا هذا إِفْكٌ مُبِينٌ): وقالوا is conjoined to ظنّ; هذا is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and إفك the khabar (predicate); مبين is a naʿt (adjective); the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The discussion of the splendid shift of person (iltifāt) in this verse will follow.
(لَوْلا جاؤُ عَلَيْهِ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَداءَ فَإِذْ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِالشُّهَداءِ): لولا is a second particle of urging, and this is the second rebuke. جاءوا is a verb and its agent; عليه is attached to شهداء; بأربعة is attached to جاءوا; شهداء is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). فإذ: the fāʾ is a conjunction and إذ is an adverb of past time attached to الكاذبون; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and jussive government; يأتوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; بالشهداء is attached to يأتوا.
[Translator's note: the source writes «حرف تخصيص» ("particle of specification"), evidently a misprint for «تحضيض» (urging), and «فاذا» for the Quranic «فإذ»; translated as intended. Earlier it also writes «تسعه» for «تسعة».]
(فَأُولئِكَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْكاذِبُونَ): the fāʾ is the connective (rābiṭa); أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; عند الله is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. in His judgement; هم is a second mubtadaʾ or a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); الكاذبون is the khabar of أولئك or the khabar of هم, and [in the latter case] the clause is the khabar of أولئك.
(وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ): the wāw is a conjunction; لولا is a particle of non-occurrence due to occurrence (imtināʿ li-wujūd); فضل الله is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is necessarily omitted. This is the third rebuke. عليكم is attached to فضل; ورحمته is conjoined to فضل; في الدنيا is attached to an omitted ḥāl; والآخرة is conjoined to الدنيا.
(لَمَسَّكُمْ فِيما أَفَضْتُمْ فِيهِ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ): the lām occurs in the apodosis of لولا; مسّكم is a verb and its direct object, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. فيما is attached to مسّكم; the clause أفضتم فيه is the ṣila (relative clause), and «ما» denotes the talk of the slander; ifāḍa is rushing headlong and plunging in. It is also valid for ما to be maṣdariyya, i.e. "would have touched you because of your rushing and plunging into the slander". فيه is attached to أفضتم; عذاب is the agent and عظيم a naʿt.
(إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ بِأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَتَقُولُونَ بِأَفْواهِكُمْ ما لَيْسَ لَكُمْ بِهِ عِلْمٌ): this is the fourth rebuke. إذ is an adverb attached to مسّكم or to أفضتم; تلقّونه is an imperfect verb from which one of its two tāʾs has been dropped; it is nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the agent and the hāʾ the direct object. Talaqqī, talaqquf and talaqqun are close in meaning [receiving, catching, picking up]. The clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it, and the meaning is: some of you relate it from others. بألسنتكم is attached to تلقّونه; وتقولون is conjoined to تلقّونه; بأفواهكم is attached to تقولون; ما is the object of تقولون; the clause ليس is the ṣila of the relative; ليس is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; لكم is its khabar; به is attached to علم; علم is the noun of ليس.
(وَتَحْسَبُونَهُ هَيِّناً وَهُوَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَظِيمٌ): وتحسبونه is an imperfect verb, its agent and its first direct object; هينا is the second direct object; the wāw is circumstantial (li-l-ḥāl); هو is a mubtadaʾ; عند الله is a ḥāl; عظيم is the khabar of هو; and the clause is circumstantial.

* Rhetoric:
1- Expressing others by "selves":
Expressing others by "selves" (al-anfus) contains the most far-reaching of subtle points and those richest in lofty meanings. First, it calls upon the believers to mutual sympathy and to directing the reproach at oneself rather than mentioning [the other] with evil; that is more conducive to winning him over and to treating him on the basis of loyalty and closeness. This is done by portraying him as one who has started to slander himself and accuse himself of an indecency that is not in him. It is related that Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī said to his wife: "Do you not see what people are saying?" She said to him: "If you were in Ṣafwān's place, would you betray the sanctity of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with something evil?" He said: "No." She said: "And if I were in ʿĀʾisha's place I would not betray him; and Ṣafwān is better than you, and ʿĀʾisha is better than me."
This is entirely correct. ʿĀʾisha's innocence is clear and self-evidently understood by every fair-minded person who understands that a woman like ʿĀʾisha would not expose herself to such suspicion in front of an army, in broad daylight, and without necessity, with a man of the Muslims who feared what a Muslim fears in such a situation — the anger of the Prophet, the anger of the Muslims and the anger of Allah. That is a trait above which a woman lesser than ʿĀʾisha in lineage, rank, character and pride would raise herself, so how much more so she, in her well-known position! This is what is understood from expressing other believers by "the self": it moved the wife of Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī to put her husband in Ṣafwān's place and herself in ʿĀʾisha's place, and then to affirm innocence and trustworthiness for herself and her husband, so that it is affirmed for Ṣafwān and ʿĀʾisha a fortiori.
Second, it is possible that the expression "selves" is literal, the intent being to bind the one who thinks ill to [the same judgement on] himself, because he did not take account of the impulses and restraints of faith in the case of others, while he found and took account of them in the case of himself, and claimed innocence for himself before knowing [the facts], by the judgement of whim, not the judgement of guidance.
2- Shift of person (iltifāt):
In the speech there is a turn from the second person to the third, and from the pronoun to the overt noun. The course of the discourse would be to say «لولا إذ سمعتموه ظننتم بأنفسكم خيرا وقلتم». Eloquence required this iltifāt and the turn from pronoun to overt noun only for emphasis in the reproach, and so that the word "faith" would be stated explicitly, indicating that sharing in it requires that no believing man believe against his brother, nor any believing woman against her sister, the words of a fault-finder or a detractor. This is what the Prophet ﷺ did, and it would have befitted the others to follow his example: he heard talk being chewed over among the hypocrites and spreading to the Muslims, indeed to the closest of his own kin — talk heard by a man like ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, in the goodness of his nature, who then saw no harm in divorce, women being many. The Prophet heard that suspicious talk and neither accepted it without proof nor rejected it without proof. It was for him either to visit his sick wife or to keep his distance from her for a while; so he visited her, with such gentleness and fairness as forbade him to confront her, in her illness, with what was stirring in his noble soul, and with such displeasure and watchful waiting as forbade him to meet her as he used to meet her when the soul was entirely clear. He kept asking after her as one who has a reproach to make, waiting for her to recover and for the proof to come to him, so that he would be wholly severe or wholly merciful. The clamour of people did not hurry him, in this painful situation, into acting at once on what jealous honour (al-ḥamiyya) requires and what chivalry (al-murūʾa) requires.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and Misṭaḥ:
If it is said that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy was one of those with tribal backing (ʿaṣabiyya) whose weight is reckoned with and whose outbursts are guarded against, what is to be said of Misṭaḥ, who was Abū Bakr's dependant and protégé, eating from his wealth? What saved him from displeasure and punishment and guaranteed him the continuance of kindness and support, were it not for the magnanimity of the noble Prophet, the magnanimity of Abū Bakr and the magnanimity of the Qur'an?
[Translator's note: the source reads «التي بحسب حسابها», evidently for «التي يُحسب حسابها» ("whose weight is reckoned with"); translated accordingly.]
3- Hyperbole (al-mubālagha):
The discussion of a similar expression, «تقولون بأفواهكم», has preceded: speech is only by the mouth, so what is the point of mentioning mouths? We repeat that here it is for emphasis and for the insinuation that one may speak glibly and pronounce with the glibness of one who is certain and knowing — which is more severe and more decisive. Its meaning is that a thing known exists with its knowledge in the heart, and the tongue expresses it; but this slander is nothing but speech that runs on your tongues and circulates in your mouths, without expressing any knowledge of it in the heart.

dervis-irab:16-20.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْلا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ قُلْتُمْ ما يَكُونُ لَنا أَنْ نَتَكَلَّمَ بِهذا): this is the fifth rebuke. لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) and reproach; إذ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) قلتم; i.e. it behoved you, at the mere first hearing, to say: "It is not fitting for us to speak of this," and to say "Glory be to You". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: How is it permissible to separate between لولا and قلتم by the adverb? I say: adverbs have a special status, namely that they are treated, in relation to things, as the things themselves, because things occur in them and are never separated from them; hence latitude is allowed with them that is not allowed with others." Abū Ḥayyān replied to him, saying: "This gives the false impression that this is specific to the adverb, whereas it applies to the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) as well: you say لولا زيدا ضربت (why did you not strike Zayd) and لولا عمرا قتلت (why did you not kill ʿAmr)." The secret of fronting the adverb will come in the section on rhetoric.
The clause سمعتموه is what the adverb is put in construct with; the clause قلتم has no grammatical position because it is initial (ibtidāʾiyya); ما is negative; يكون is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; لنا is its fronted khabar (predicate); أن and what follows it is its postponed noun; بهذا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نتكلم; سبحانك is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the clause سبحانك is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because its meaning is wonder; the meaning is: why did you not say "It is not fitting for us to speak of this", in the state of being amazed at this strange, astonishing matter.
[Translator's note: in this paraphrase the source has «أن تتكلم», evidently for «أن نتكلم» as in the verse; translated accordingly.]
(سُبْحانَكَ هذا بُهْتانٌ عَظِيمٌ): هذا is the mubtadaʾ (subject), بهتان the khabar, and عظيم a naʿt (adjective).
(يَعِظُكُمُ اللَّهُ أَنْ تَعُودُوا لِمِثْلِهِ أَبَداً إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): this is the sixth rebuke. يعظكم has been made to include (ḍummina) the meaning of a verb made transitive by عن, then the preposition was omitted, i.e. He forbids you from returning. It is an imperfect verb and its direct object; الله is the fāʿil (agent); أن and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition; لمثله is attached to تعودوا; أبدا is an adverb of time, also attached to تعودوا. It is also said that there is no implied inclusion (taḍmīn) in the meaning of يعظكم, and that أن and what follows it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "out of aversion to your returning". إن is conditional; كنتم is kāna and its noun; مؤمنين is its khabar; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. if you are believers, then do not return to the like of it.
(وَيُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآياتِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; يبين الله is a verb and its agent; لكم is attached to يبين; الآيات is the direct object; الله is a mubtadaʾ and عليم حكيم are two khabars of الله.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحِبُّونَ أَنْ تَشِيعَ الْفاحِشَةُ فِي الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): a resumptive clause, brought to present the seventh rebuke. إنّ and its noun; the clause يحبون is the ṣila (relative clause); أن and what follows it is the object of يحبون; الفاحشة is the agent [of تشيع]; في الذين آمنوا is attached to تشيع.
(لَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ): لهم is a fronted khabar and عذاب a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ; أليم is a naʿt; في الدنيا والآخرة is a second naʿt. In this world it was established by the ḥadd (prescribed penalty) for slander (qadhf); the details of this will come in the section on benefits. الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يعلم its khabar; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا تعلمون its khabar.
(وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ رَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ): this is the eighth rebuke. لولا is of non-occurrence (imtināʿiyya); فضل الله عليكم is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is necessarily omitted; ورحمته is conjoined to فضل; وأن الله رءوف رحيم is conjoined to فضل الله; and the apodosis of لولا is omitted, i.e. He would have hastened punishment upon you.

* Benefits:
It is established that the Prophet ﷺ applied the ḥadd to the four slanderers: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, Ḥassān ibn Thābit, Misṭaḥ and Ḥamna bint Jaḥsh. Ṣafwān lay in wait for Ḥassān ibn Thābit and struck him with the sword, and blinded him; about this he says:
توّق ذباب السيف عني فإنني ... غلام إذا هو جيت لست بشاعر
ولكنني أحمي حماي وأتقى ... من الباهت الرامي البريء الظواهر
(Take the edge of the sword from me, for I am a young man who, when lampooned, is no poet; but I defend what is mine to protect, and I take revenge on the slanderer who accuses the outwardly innocent.)
Ḥassān ibn Thābit recited verses in which he praised the Mother of the Believers ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and cleared her of what had been attributed to her, among them:
حصان رزان ما تزنّ بريبة ... وتصبح غرثى من لحوم الغوافل
حليلة خير الناس دينا ومنصبا ... نبيّ الهدى والمكرمات الفواضل
عقيلة حي من لؤي بن غالب ... كرام المساعي مجدها غير زائل
مهذّبة قد طيب الله جنيها ... وطهرها من كل شين وباطل
فإن كان ما بلغت عني قلته ... فلا رفعت سوطي إليّ أناملي
وكيف وودي ما حييت ونصرتي ... بآل رسول الله زين المحافل
له رتب عال على الناس فضلها ... تقاصر عنها سورة المتطاول
(Chaste and composed, she is not suspected of any doubtful matter, and she rises hungry for the flesh of heedless women [i.e. she backbites no one]; wife of the best of people in religion and rank, the Prophet of guidance and of abundant noble deeds; the noblest lady of a clan of Luʾayy ibn Ghālib, noble in their endeavours, whose glory does not fade; refined — Allah has made her nature good and purified her of every blemish and falsehood. If I said what you were told I said, then may my fingers never lift my whip to me. How could that be, when my love as long as I live and my support are for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of assemblies? He has ranks high above people in excellence, beneath which the ascent of the aspirant falls short.)
[Translator's note: the source prints these verses with the line divisions displaced (e.g. «غير / زائل», «الم / حافل»); they are given here in their proper verse order without changing any word. «هو جيت» is a print-split of «هوجيت».]

* Rhetoric:
1- Fronting and postponing (al-taqdīm wa-l-taʾkhīr):
In His words, Exalted is He, «وَلَوْلا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ قُلْتُمْ …», the adverb is fronted for an important benefit: to show that it was obligatory upon them to refrain from speaking of the slander as soon as they first heard it. Since mentioning the time was more important, fronting was required. ʿAbd al-Qāhir has a discussion in Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz on fronting and postponing, in which he says: the chapter of fronting and postponing is one of the chapters through which the excellence of speech appears, by which one style rises above another, and through which the inimitability of the Qur'an becomes manifest.
2- The secret of the exclamation:
In the word of wonder «سبحانك» there is a wonderful secret: originally Allah is glorified upon seeing something wondrous among His works; then it became frequent until it was used upon anything that is wondered at.

dervis-irab:45-49.t:
* I'rab:
(وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ ماءٍ) A resumptive statement set out to explain the kinds of creation. (الله) is the mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause (خلق) is the khabar (predicate), (كل دابة) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (من ماء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلق), i.e. a drop of sperm, according to what is most common. (فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى بَطْنِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى رِجْلَيْنِ) The fāʾ is ramifying (tafrīʿiyya); (منهم) is a fronted khabar and (من) a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause (يمشي) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (على بطنه) is attached to (يمشي); and (ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين) is conjoined to what precedes it. (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى أَرْبَعٍ) Conjoined. The secret of using (من) for non-rational beings will come in the section on rhetoric.
(يَخْلُقُ اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) (يخلق الله ما يشاء): an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila. (إن الله): inna and its noun; (على كل شيء) is attached to (قدير), and (قدير) is the khabar of inna. (لَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنا آياتٍ مُبَيِّناتٍ وَاللَّهُ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) A resumptive statement set out to mention His signs, Glorified is He, by way of iltifāt (shift of address), as will come in the section on rhetoric. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (أنزلنا) is a verb and its agent; (آيات) is the mafʿūl bihi and (مبينات) an adjective.
