On the lightened reading «مِنْ أحد» is the agent; on the doubled reading it is the object. And «مِنْ» is redundant on both views. The agent is Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ يَأْتَلِ}: it may be «يَفْتَعِلُ» from «الأَلِيَّة», which is the oath, as in the verse:
3437 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . .
وآلَتْ حَلْفَةً لم تَحَلَّلِ
("and she swore an oath that she did not absolve").
Al-Zamakhsharī supported this with the reading of al-Ḥasan «ولا يَتَأَلَّ» from «الأَلِيَّة», as in the [ḥadīth] "whoever takes an oath against Allah, He will give him the lie". It may also be «يَفْتَعِلُ» from «أَلَوْتُ», i.e. "I fell short", as in the saying of the Exalted {لاَ يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبَالاً} [Āl ʿImrān: 118]. He said:
3438 - وما المرءُ ما دامَتْ حُشاشةُ نَفْسِه ... بمُدْرِكِ أَطْراف الخُطوب ولا آلِ
("A man, so long as a spark of life remains in him, neither attains the extremities of calamities nor falls short.")
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«ولا يَتَأَلَّ» has also been read, on the pattern yatafaʿʿal, and it is from «الأَلِيَّة» too."
I say: and from it:
3439 - تَأَلَّى ابنُ أَوْسٍ حَلْفَةً لِيَرُدَّني ... إلى نِسْوةٍ كأنَّهنَّ مَفائِدُ
("Ibn Aws swore an oath to return me to women who are like spits for roasting.")
His saying: {أَن يؤتوا}: it is on the dropping of the preposition, and its implied form on the first view is «ولا يَأْتَلِ أُولوو الفَضْلِ على أَنْ لا يُحِسنوا» ("let not those of virtue swear not to do good"); on the second: «ولا يُقَصِّر أُولو الفَضْل في أَنْ يُحِسنوا» ("let not those of virtue fall short in doing good"). Abū Ḥaywa, Abū l-Barhasam and Ibn Quṭayb read «تُؤْتُوا» with the tāʾ of address. It is an iltifāt that agrees with His saying «ألا تُحِبون». Al-Ḥasan and Sufyān ibn al-Ḥusayn read «وَلْتَعْفُوا وَلْتَصْفَحُوا» in the second person, which agrees with what follows it.

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ}: its governor is the settling (istiqrār) to which «لهم» is attached. It is also said: rather its governor is «عذابُ». This was rejected because it is a described maṣdar, and it was answered that latitude is allowed in the adverbial that is not allowed in other things. The two brothers read «يَشْهَدُ» with the yāʾ (masculine), because the feminine is figurative and a separation has occurred. The rest [read it] with the tāʾ, in regard to the wording.

semin-durr:25-25.t: The tanwīn in «إذ» is a substitute for a clause, its implied form being «يوم إذ تشهد» ("the day when it testifies"). The disagreement of al-Akhfash about it has already been given. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يُوْفِيْهِمْ» lightened, from «أوفى». The majority read «الحق» in the accusative as an adjective of «دينَهم», while Abū Ḥaywa, Abū Rawq and Mujāhid, and it is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd, read it in the nominative as an adjective of Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ}: it may be a resumptive clause, or in the nominative position as a second khabar; and it may be that «لهم» is the khabar of «أولئك» and «مغفرةٌ» its agent.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {تَسْتَأْنِسُواْ}: it may be from «الاستئناس» (seeking familiarity), because the one who knocks feels uneasy about whether he will be admitted or not, so his unease is removed; it is a synonym of asking permission, and so was put in its place. It is also said: from «الإيناس», which is perceiving, i.e. "until you find out the state of affairs". Ibn ʿAbbās explained it as «حتى تَسْتَأْذِنُوا» ("until you ask permission"), but that is not a reading. What is transmitted from him, that he said: "«تستأنسوا» is a scribe's mistake; it is only «تستأذنوا»" . . . . . is falsely ascribed to him. It is parallel to what was given earlier in [Sūrat] al-Raʿd, {أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الذين آمنوا} [al-Raʿd: 31], about which the discussion has been given.
[Translator's note: the source reads «إنما هون تستأذنوا»; «هون» is evidently a misprint for «هو».]
«والاستِئْناسُ» is seeking information. He said:
3440 - كأنَّ رَحْلِيْ وقد زال النهارُ بنا ... يومَ الجليلِ على مُسْتَأْنِسٍ وَحَِدِ
("As if my saddle, when the day had declined with us on the day of al-Jalīl, were on a wary, solitary [wild ox]").
It is also said: it is from «الإنْس» with kasra on the hamza, i.e. he finds out whether there is a human being in it or not. Al-Ṭabarī reported that it means «وتُؤْنِسُوا أنفسَكم» ("and put your selves at ease").
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The conjugation of the verb refuses to let it be from «آنسَ»."

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {أَن تَدْخُلُواْ}: i.e. «في أن تدخلوا» ("in that you enter"). The preposition phrase is attached to «جُناح».

semin-durr:30-30.t: His saying: {مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ}: there are several views about «مِنْ». The first: that it is partitive, because the first glance that occurs without intention is pardoned for the one looking. The second: that it is for stating the kind; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this, and there is something to consider in it, in that no vague term has preceded for «مِنْ» to explain. The third: that it is for the beginning of the range; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The fourth: that it is redundant; this is the statement of al-Akhfash.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {وَلْيَضْرِبْنَ}: «يَضْرِبْنَ» includes the meaning of «يُلْقِيْنَ» ("cast"), which is why it is made transitive by «على». Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read the imperative lām with kasra.
Ṭalḥa read «بخُمْرِهنَّ» with sukūn on the mīm; giving sukūn to [the pattern] fuʿul in the plural is preferable to giving sukūn to the singular. Ibn Kathīr, the two brothers and Ibn Dhakwān put kasra on the jīm of «جُيُوْبِهِنَّ».
«والغَضُّ» is the closing of the eyelid so that it prevents seeing. He said:
3441 - فَغُضِّ الطَرْفَ إنَّك مِنْ نُمَيْرٍ ... فلا كعباً بَلَغْتَ ولا كِلابا
("So lower your gaze, for you are of Numayr; you have reached neither Kaʿb nor Kilāb.")
«والخُمُر» is the plural of «خِمار». In the paucal it is pluralised as «أَخْمِرَة». Imruʾ al-Qays said:
3442 - وَتَرى الشَّجْراءَ في رَيِّقِهِ ... كَرُؤوسِ قُطِعَتْ فيها الخُمُرْ
("And you see the trees in its first flush like heads that have been cut off, with the head-coverings still on them.")
«والجَيْب» is what is in the collar of the shirt, from which part of the body shows.
His saying: {غَيْرِ أُوْلِي}: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read «غيرَ» in the accusative. There are two views on it: the first, that it is an exception; the second, that it is a ḥāl. The rest [read] «غيرِ» in the genitive as an adjective, or a badal, or a bayān. «والإِرْبَةُ» is need. Its derivation was given in [Sūrat] Ṭāhā.
His saying: {مِنَ الرجال}: a ḥāl from «أُولي». As for His saying «أو الطفلِ الذين», it was given in [Sūrat] al-Ḥajj that «الطفلَ» applies to the dual and the plural, which is why it was described in the plural. It is also said: since the class was intended, the plural was observed in it; so it is like their saying «أهلكَ الناسَ الدينارُ الحُمْرُ والدِّرْهَمُ البيضُ» ("the red dinars and the white dirhams have ruined people").
«وعَوْرات» is the plural of «عَوْرَة», which is what a person wishes to cover of his body, and it predominantly applies to the two private parts. The majority read «عَوْرات» with sukūn on the wāw, which is the dialect of the generality of the Arabs; they gave it sukūn for lightness, because of the weak letter. Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission read «عَوَرات» with fatḥa on the ʿayn [sic: the wāw]. Ibn Khālawayh reported that it is the reading of Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Aʿmash. It is the dialect of Hudhayl ibn Mudrika. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Some recited to me:
3443 - أخُو بَيَضاتٍ رائِحٌ متأوِّبُ ... رفيقٌ بمَسحِ المَنْكِبَيْنِ سَبُوحُ
("[A male ostrich,] father of eggs, going out in the evening and returning, gentle in stroking the two shoulders, swift-gliding.")
Ibn Mujāhid considered it a solecism and a mistake, meaning from the standpoint of transmission; otherwise it is an established dialect.
His saying: {أَيُّهَا المؤمنون}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the hāʾ and an alif after the hāʾ, being the «ها» of attention. Ibn ʿĀmir here, in [Sūrat] al-Zukhruf {ياأيها الساحر} [verse 49] and in [Sūrat] al-Raḥmān {أَيُّهَا الثقلان} [verse 31] read it with ḍamma on the hāʾ in continuous reading, and when he pauses he gives it sukūn. The reason: when the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, the fatḥa on a light letter was felt to be light, so the hāʾ was given ḍamma by assimilation. These three places have been written without an alif. Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī pause with an alif, and the rest without it, following the script and the agreement of writing with pronunciation; and it is retained elsewhere, in keeping with the original, as in {يَاأَيُّهَا الناس} [al-Baqara: 21] and {يَآأَيُّهَا الذين آمَنُواْ} [al-Baqara: 153]. In sum, the script is a followed tradition.
[Translator's note: in the second paragraph on «عَوَرات», the source says "fatḥa on the ʿayn", although the fatḥa that distinguishes this form falls on the wāw; the text is translated as printed.]

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {الأيامى}: the plural of «أيِّم», on the pattern fayʿil. From it one says «آمَ يَئِيْم», like «باع يبيع». The poet said:
3444 - كلُّ امرىءٍ سَتَئِيْمُ مِنْهُ ... العِرْسُ أو منها يَئِيْمُ
("Every man — his wife will become widowed of him, or he will become widowed of her.")
The regular plural of it would be «أيائم», like «سَيِّد» and «سِيائِد». As for «أيامى» there are two views. The more apparent, from the speech of Sībawayh, is that it is a plural on the pattern fiʿālā, not transposed, and likewise «يتامى». It is also said: the original is «أيايِم» and «يتايِم» for «أيِّم» and «يتيم», and they were transposed. «والأَيِّم» is one who has no spouse, male or female. Abū Bakr al-Khaffāf restricted it to a woman who has lost her husband, so its application to a virgin is figurative. «منكم» is a ḥāl, and likewise «مِنْ عبادِكم».

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {والذين يَبْتَغُونَ الْكِتَابَ}: the nominative is possible in it, as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar the clause joined with the fāʾ, because of the sense of condition that the mubtadaʾ includes. Its accusative is also possible, by an implied verb, on the basis of ishtighāl. This is preferable because of the imperative.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«آم» and «آمَتْ» and «تَأَيَّما» are said when the two have not married, whether both are virgins or previously married. He said:
3445 - فإن تنكِحي أنكِحْ وإن تتأيَّمي ... وإن كنتُ أفتى منكمُ أتَأَيَّمُ
('If you marry, I shall marry; and if you remain unmarried, I shall remain unmarried, though I am younger than you.')
And from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'O Allah, we seek refuge in You from ʿayma, ghayma, ayma, kazam and qaram.'" I say: as for «العَيْمَة» with the undotted ʿayn, it is intense craving for milk, and with the dotted ghayn [«الغَيْمة»] intense thirst. «والأَيْمة» is a long period of celibacy; «والكَزَم» is intense craving for eating; and «والقَرَمُ» is intense craving for meat.
His saying: {عَلَى البغآء}: «البغاء» is the maṣdar of «بَغَت المرأةُ تَبْغي بِغاءً», i.e. she committed fornication. It is specific to women's fornication. This condition has no implied contrary meaning, because compulsion does not coexist with willingness.
His saying: {فِإِنَّ الله}: a clause that occurs as the apodosis of the condition. The returning pronoun to the conditional noun is omitted, its implied form being «غفور لهم» ("forgiving to them"). Al-Zamakhsharī implied it in one of his implications, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū l-Baqāʾ [implied]: «فإنَّ اللهَ غفورٌ لهنَّ», i.e. for the women who are compelled; so the clause of the consequence is bare of a link tying it to the conditional noun. It is not said that the link is the implied pronoun that is the agent of the maṣdar, since the implied form is «مِن بعد إكراهِهم لهنَّ», so that this implied link would suffice; because they did not count that among the links. You say «هندٌ عجبْتُ مِنْ ضَرْبِها زيداً», and this is permissible; but if you said «هندٌ عجبتُ مِنْ ضَرْبِ زيدٍ», i.e. from her striking, it would be impermissible, because of its lacking a link even though it is implied.
Imām al-Rāzī weakened the implication of «بهم» and preferred the implication of «بهنَّ», saying: "There are two views on it. The first: forgiving to them (the women), because compulsion removes sin and punishment from the compelled person in what he did. The second: Allah is forgiving to the one who compels, on condition of repentance. This is weak, because on the first interpretation there is no need for this implication." There is something to consider in this, as you have learned that, according to the majority, a pronoun returning to the conditional noun is necessary, and its investigation was given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara. When al-Zamakhsharī implied «لهنَّ» he raised a question, saying: "If you say: there is no need to attach the forgiveness to them, because the woman compelled to fornication, unlike the one who compels [her to it], is not sinful. I say: perhaps the compulsion is something other than what the Sharia has taken into account, of compulsion by killing or by what one fears destruction or loss of a limb from, so that she is safe from sin. Perhaps she fell short of the limit within which she is excused, and so is sinful."

semin-durr:34-34.t:
The disagreement over «مُبَيّنات», with kasra and fatḥa, has already been given.
His saying: {وَمَثَلاً}: a conjunction upon «آيات», i.e. "and We sent down an example from the examples of those before you".

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {الله نُورُ السماوات}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar, either on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. «ذو نورِ السماوات» ("the possessor of the light of the heavens"), the light meaning His justice. His saying {مَثَلُ نُورِهِ} supports this. He annexed the light to these two containers, either as an indication of the breadth of His radiance and the spread of His illumination, so that the heavens and the earth are lit by it, or in order to mean the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, who are illumined by it. It is also possible that the expression is exaggerated by way of praise, as in their saying: "So-and-so is the sun of the lands and their moon." Al-Nābigha said:
3446 - فإنَّك شمسٌ والملوكُ كواكبٌ ... إذا ظهرَتْ لم يَبْدُ منهنَّ كوكبُ
("For you are a sun and the kings are stars; when it appears, not one of them shows.")
And he said:
3447 - قَمَر القبائلِ خالدُ بن يزيد ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
("The moon of the tribes is Khālid ibn Yazīd ...")
It is also possible that the maṣdar occurs in place of the active participle, i.e. «مُنَوِّرُ السماواتِ» ("illuminator of the heavens"). This view is supported by the reading of the Commander of the Faithful, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Jaʿfar and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Makkī: «نَوَّرَ» as a past verb, its agent the pronoun of the Creator the Exalted, «السماواتِ» its object, so its kasra is the accusative sign, and «الأرضَ» in the accusative is conjoined to it. Al-Ḥasan explained it, saying: "Allah is the illuminator of the heavens."
His saying: {مَثَلُ نُورِهِ كَمِشْكَاةٍ}: also a mubtadaʾ and khabar. This clause is a clarification and explanation of what precedes it, so it has no position. There is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «كَمَثَلِ نورِ مشْكاة». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. the description of His light, wondrous in its illumination, is like a niche, i.e. like the description of a niche."
They disagreed about the pronoun in «نُوره». It is said: it is for Allah the Exalted, and this is preferable, and the light on this view means the clear verses mentioned earlier, or faith. It is also said: it refers to the believers, or the believer, or whoever believed in Him. Ubayy read with all these wordings, and he returned the pronoun to what he read. It is also said: it refers to Muḥammad ﷺ, though no mention of these things has preceded. As for its referring to the believers in Ubayy's reading, there is a difficulty in respect of the singular. Makkī said: "One pauses at «الأرض» on these three views."
They also disagreed about this simile: is it a composite simile (tashbīh murakkab), i.e. the intention is to compare a whole with a whole, without regard to matching part with part, but the intention is to compare His guidance and the perfection of His craft in every created thing, as a whole, with this whole of the light that they make, which is the most eloquent attribute of light among you? Or a non-composite simile, i.e. the intention is to match part with part? The discussion about it is arranged according to the views on the pronoun in «نوره».
«والمِشْكاةُ» is a niche that does not go through. Is it Arabic, or Abyssinian and Arabicised? There is disagreement. It is also said: it is the iron or lead [vessel] in which the wick (dhubāl) is placed, and it is in the interior of the glass. It is also said: it is the pillar on whose top the lamp is placed. And it is said: the iron thing in which the lantern is hung. Al-Dūrī from al-Kisāʾī used imāla in «المِشْكاة» because of the preceding kasra, even though there is a separator. It is written with a wāw, like «الزكاة» and «الصلاة».
«والمِصْباح» is the large lamp. «والزجاجةُ» is the singular of «الزجاج», a well-known substance. It has three dialects: ḍamma is the dialect of the Hijaz and the reading of the majority; kasra and fatḥa are the dialect of Qays. Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim, in Ibn Mujāhid's transmission, read it with fatḥa. Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim in another transmission from him, and Abū Rajāʾ, read it with kasra. The disagreement is likewise in His saying «الزجاجةُ».
The clause of His saying {فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ} is an adjective of «مِشْكاة». It is also possible that the preposition phrase alone is the description and «مصباحٌ» is nominative by it as agent.
His saying: {دُرِّيٌّ}: Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read it with kasra on the dāl and a yāʾ followed by a hamza. Ḥamza and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read it with ḍamma on the dāl and a yāʾ followed by a hamza. The rest [read it] with ḍamma on the dāl and a doubled yāʾ without hamza. These three are among the Seven. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda read it with fatḥa on the dāl and a doubled yāʾ. Al-Zuhrī read it with kasra on it and a doubled yāʾ. Abān ibn ʿUthmān, Ibn al-Musayyab, Abū Rajāʾ and also Qatāda read «دَرِّيْء» with fatḥa on the dāl, a doubled rā᾽ and a yāʾ followed by a hamza.
As for the first, it is a clear reading because it is a pattern found often in nouns, such as «سِكِّين», and in adjectives, such as «سِكِّير».
As for the second reading, it is from «الدِّرْء», meaning pushing, i.e. its parts push one another, or its light pushes away its concealment. It is said that nothing is found on the pattern fuʿʿīl except «مُرِّيْق» (for safflower), and «سُرِّيَّة», on our view that it comes from «السرور», a yāʾ having been substituted for one of the doubled letters and the yāʾ of fuʿʿīl assimilated into it; and «مُرِّيخ» (for what is inside a dry horn), also said with kasra on the mīm; and «عُلِّيَّة», and «دُرِّيْء» in this reading, and «ذُرِّيَّة» too in one view. Some said: "The pattern of «دُرِّيْء» in this reading is fuʿʿūl, like «سُبُّوح» and «قُدُّوس»; the succession of ḍammas was felt heavy so it was shifted to kasra, and this is also transmitted in «سُرِّية» and «ذُرِّيَّة»."
As for the third reading, it admits two views. The first: that its origin has the hamza as in Ḥamza's reading, except that he substituted a yāʾ for the hamza and assimilated, so that the meaning of the two readings is one. It may also be a relational form (nisba) to «الدُّر» (pearl), for its purity and the clarity of its radiance.
As for the reading with a doubled yāʾ with fatḥa and kasra on the dāl, what appears is that it is related to «الدُّر»; the fatḥa and kasra on the dāl belong to the changes of nisba forms.
As for fatḥa on the dāl with madd and hamza, there is a difficulty in it. Abū l-Fatḥ said: "It is a rare pattern, of which only «السَّكِّينة» is preserved, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and doubling of the ʿayn." I say: and al-Akhfash reported: «فَعَلَيْه السَّكِّينة والوَقار» and «كوكَبٌ دَرِّيْءٌ» from «دَرَأْتُه».
His saying: {يُوقَدُ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «تَوَقَّدَ» on the pattern tafaʿʿala, a past verb in which there is a pronoun of its agent referring to the lamp, and not to «كوكب», because the meaning would be spoiled. The two brothers and Abū Bakr [read] «تُوْقَدُ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ (feminine) and fatḥa on the qāf, the imperfect of «أَوْقَدَ». It is passive, and the deputy agent is a pronoun referring to «زجاجة» that is latent in the verb. The rest of the Seven read likewise, except with the yāʾ (masculine); and the latent pronoun refers to the lamp.
Al-Ḥasan, al-Sulamī and Ibn Muḥayṣin read, and it is related from ʿĀṣim through al-Mufaḍḍal, likewise, except that he put ḍamma on the dāl, making it the imperfect of «تَوَقَّدَ»; the original is «تَتَوَقَّد» with two tāʾs, and one of them was dropped like «تَذَكَّرُ». The pronoun is also for the glass.
ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «وَقَّدَ», a past verb on the pattern of «قَتَّلَ», doubled, i.e. the lamp. Al-Ḥasan and Sallām also read «يَوَقَّدُ» with yāʾ and ḍamma on the dāl, the imperfect of «تَوَقَّدَ». The original is «يَتَوَقَّدُ» with yāʾ and tāʾ, and the tāʾ was dropped. This is irregular, since two identical letters did not occur in succession, and nothing remained in the wording to indicate what was dropped, unlike «تَنَزَّلُ» and «تَذَكَّرُ» and their type, in which there are two tāʾs and what remains indicates what is lost. A line of analogy may be strained to justify it, namely that they carried «أَعِدُ» and «تَعِدُ» and «نَعِدُ» over «يَعِدُ» in the omission of the wāw because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra; likewise they carried «يَتَوَقَّد» with yāʾ and tāʾ over «تَتَوَقَّد» with two tāʾs, even though the heaviness is not found in the yāʾ and tāʾ.
His saying: {مِن شَجَرَةٍ}: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range, and there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «مِنْ زيتِ شجرةٍ» ("from the oil of a tree"). Concerning «زَيْتونة» there are two views, of which the better known is that it is a badal from «شجرةٍ». The second: that it is an ʿaṭf bayān; this is the school of the Kufans, and Abū ʿAlī followed them. This has already been given at His saying {مِن مَّآءٍ صَدِيدٍ} [Ibrāhīm: 16].
His saying: {لاَّ شَرْقِيَّةٍ}: an adjective of «شَجَرة», and the «لا» entered to convey negation. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read it in the nominative, on the implication of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. «لا هي شرقيةٌ» ("it is not eastern"). The clause is also in the genitive position as an adjective of «شَجَرة».
His saying: {يَكَادُ}: this clause is also an adjective of «شجرةٍ».
His saying: {وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ}: its apodosis is omitted, i.e. «لأضاءَتْ» ("it would give light"), because of the indication of what precedes it, and the clause is a ḥāl clause. The investigation of this was given at the saying «رُدُّوا السَّائلَ ولو جاءَ على فَرَس» ("Turn the beggar away, even if he comes on a horse"), and that it is for covering all the states, even in this state. Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan read «يَمْسَسْه» with the yāʾ (masculine), because the feminine is figurative and because there is also a separation by the object.
His saying: {نُّورٌ على نُورٍ}: the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. «ذلك نورٌ» ("that is light"). And «على نورٍ» is an adjective of «نور».

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (سُورَةٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهَا وَفَرَضْنَاهَا وَأَنْزَلْنَا فِيهَا آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ (١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سُورَةٌ): in the nominative, on the implied wording: "this is a sūra" (هَذِهِ سُورَةٌ), or "among what is recited to you is a sūra" (مِمَّا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكَ سُورَةٌ).
سورة cannot be a mubtadaʾ (subject), because it is indefinite. It has also been read in the accusative, on the implied wording "We sent down a sūra" (أَنْزَلْنَا سُورَةً); on this reading «أَنْزَلْنَاهَا» has no grammatical position, because it explains something that has no position, so it has no position itself.
The accusative is also possible on the implied wording "mention a sūra" (اذْكُرْ سُورَةً); then the position of «أَنْزَلْنَاهَا» is accusative, while on the nominative reading its position is nominative.
(وَفَرَضْنَاهَا) with doubling (tashdīd) is because it denotes the multitude of obligations it contains, or the emphasis on the obligation to act on what it contains; and without doubling it has the meaning "We made acting on what is in it obligatory".

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الزَّانِيَةُ وَالزَّانِي فَاجْلِدُوا كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ وَلَا تَأْخُذْكُمْ بِهِمَا رَأْفَةٌ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ (١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الزَّانِيَةُ وَالزَّانِي): there are two views on its nominative:
The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "and among what is recited to you are the female fornicator and the male fornicator" (وَفِيمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكَ الزَّانِيَةُ وَالزَّانِي); on this view (فَاجْلِدُوا) is resumptive. The second: the khabar is (فَاجْلِدُوا).
It has also been read in the accusative, by a verb indicated by (فَاجْلِدُوا); we have dealt with this exhaustively at His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاللَّذَانِ يَأْتِيَانِهَا مِنْكُمْ).
And (مِائَةَ) and (وَثَمَانِينَ) are both accusative in the manner of maṣdars (verbal nouns).
(وَلَا تَأْخُذْكُمْ بِهِمَا): the bāʾ cannot be attached (mutaʿalliq) to (رَأْفَةً) [Translator's note: so in the source, in the accusative, although the verse has رَأْفَةٌ in the nominative.], because a maṣdar's dependent cannot precede it; it is attached only to تأخذ, i.e. "and let it not seize you on their account" (وَلَا تَأْخُذْكُمْ بِسَبَبِهِمَا).
It may also be attached to something omitted, by way of clarification (bayān), i.e. "I mean, towards them" (أَعْنِي بِهِمَا), that is, "do not be compassionate towards them", and the maṣdar explains it.
الرأفة has four forms: with a sukūn on the hamza and with a fatḥa on it, with the hamza replaced by an alif, and with an alif added after it; all of these are dialectal forms, and it has been read with each of them.
And (فِي) is attached to تأخذكم.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَاءَ فَاجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً وَلَا تَقْبَلُوا لَهُمْ شَهَادَةً أَبَدًا وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ): there are two views on its position:
The first is the nominative, and the other the accusative, as was mentioned at His saying, Exalted is He: (الزَّانِيَةُ وَالزَّانِي).
(فَاجْلِدُوهُمْ), i.e. "flog each one of them" (فَاجْلِدُوا كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ); the muḍāf was omitted.
(وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ): a resumptive clause, and it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا): this is an exception from the clauses preceding it according to one group, and from the clause immediately before it according to others. The position of the excepted is accusative, according to the basic rule of the chapter. It is also said that its position is genitive as a badal (substitute) of the pronoun in «لَهُمْ».
It is also said that its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being «فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ», with an omitted pronoun in the khabar, i.e. "forgiving towards them" (غَفُورٌ لَهُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أَزْوَاجَهُمْ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ شُهَدَاءُ إِلَّا أَنْفُسُهُمْ فَشَهَادَةُ أَحَدِهِمْ أَرْبَعُ شَهَادَاتٍ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا أَنْفُسُهُمْ): it is a naʿt (adjective) of شهداء, or a badal (substitute) of it.
Had it been read in the accusative, that would have been permissible, as the khabar of كان, or as an exception. The nominative is stronger only because «إِلَّا» here is an adjective of the indefinite noun, as we mentioned in Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ at His saying, Exalted is He: (لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا).
(فَشَهَادَةُ أَحَدِهِمْ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its agent. There are two views on its nominative. The first: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then what is obligatory is the testimony of one of them" (فَالْوَاجِبُ شَهَادَةُ أَحَدِهِمْ). The second: it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, i.e. "then incumbent upon them is the testimony of one of them" (فَعَلَيْهِمْ شَهَادَةُ أَحَدِهِمْ).
And (أَرْبَعَ) is in the accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "that one of them testify four" (أَنْ يَشْهَدَ أَحَدُهُمْ أَرْبَعَ).
And (بِاللَّهِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to شهادات according to the Basrans, because it is nearer, and to «شَهَادَةُ» according to the Kufans, because it is the first of the two operators.
And (إِنَّهُ) together with what it governs is the dependent of شهادات, or of شهادة, according to what we mentioned, i.e. "he testifies that he is truthful"; but the operator has been suspended (ʿulliqa) because of the lām in the khabar, and for that reason إنّ is given a kasra.
Its position is either accusative or genitive, according to the difference between the two schools concerning «أَنَّ» when the preposition before it is omitted.
«أَرْبَعُ» is also read in the nominative, as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; on this reading the mubtadaʾ can have no governing effect on anything after the khabar, so as not to separate the ṣila from the relative [Translator's note: i.e. the maṣdar from its dependent, the maṣdar being treated like a relative noun]; so it is necessary that شهادات govern what comes after it.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالْخَامِسَةُ أَنَّ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْخَامِسَةُ), i.e. "and the fifth testimony"; it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is «أَنَّ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ».
It is also read with «أَنَّ» without doubling; it is then the lightened form of the heavy one, and its noun is omitted.
And (مِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ) is the khabar of «أَنَّ» on the reading with doubling, and the khabar of «لَعْنَةُ» on the reading without doubling. [Translator's note: so in the source; the phrase normally given as the khabar here is عَلَيْهِ, while مِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ is the khabar of كان.]
«وَالْخَامِسَةَ» is also read in the accusative, on the implied wording "and he testifies the fifth" (وَيَشْهَدُ الْخَامِسَةَ); the implied wording then is "that the curse of Allah…" (بِأَنَّ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ), and it may also be a badal (substitute) of الخامسة.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَدْرَأُ عَنْهَا الْعَذَابَ أَنْ تَشْهَدَ أَرْبَعَ شَهَادَاتٍ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تَشْهَدَ): it is the fāʿil (agent) of يدرأ.
And (بِاللَّهِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to شهادات, or to أن تشهد, as we mentioned in the first one.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالْخَامِسَةَ أَنَّ غَضَبَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْخَامِسَةَ أَنَّ غَضَبَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا): it is like the first الخامسة. «أَنَّ» is read with doubling, and «أَنْ» without doubling with «غَضَبُ» in the nominative; and it is also read غَضِبَ, as a verb.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ حَكِيمٌ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ): the answer of «لَوْلَا» is omitted, its implied form being "you would have perished" (لَهَلَكْتُمْ) or "you would have been brought out" (لَخَرَجْتُمْ); and like it is the head of the twentieth verse of this sūra.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جَاءُوا بِالْإِفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِنْكُمْ لَا تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرًّا لَكُمْ بَلْ هُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ مَا اكْتَسَبَ مِنَ الْإِثْمِ وَالَّذِي تَوَلَّى كِبْرَهُ مِنْهُمْ لَهُ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ (١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عُصْبَةٌ مِنْكُمْ): it is the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ», and منكم is a naʿt (adjective) of it; it is through this that the khabar becomes informative.
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا تَحْسَبُوهُ): resumptive; the hāʾ is the pronoun of the slander (الإفك), or of the accusation (القذف).
And (كِبْرَهُ) with kasra means "the greater part of it"; and with ḍamma it is from their saying: "the walāʾ (right of clientage) belongs to the eldest" (الْوَلَاءُ لِلْكُبْرِ), the كُبْر being the eldest of a man's children; i.e. "he took charge of the greatest of it" (تَوَلَّى أَكْبَرَهُ).

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ بِأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَتَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَاهِكُمْ مَا لَيْسَ لَكُمْ بِهِ عِلْمٌ وَتَحْسَبُونَهُ هَيِّنًا وَهُوَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَظِيمٌ (١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ): the operator governing «إِذْ» is مسّكم, or أفضتم.
It is also read تُلْقُونَهُ, with ḍamma on the tāʾ, from أَلْقَيْتُ الشَّيْءَ, "I threw the thing", when you cast it away. And تَلِقُونَهُ, with fatḥa on the tāʾ, kasra on the lām and ḍamma on the qāf without doubling, i.e. "you hasten in it"; its origin is from الوَلَق, which is madness.
It is also read تَقَفَّوْنَهُ, with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the qāf and a doubled fāʾ with a fatḥa after it; its original form is تَتَقَفَّوْنَ, i.e. "you follow".

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَعِظُكُمُ اللَّهُ أَنْ تَعُودُوا لِمِثْلِهِ أَبَدًا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ (١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تَعُودُوا), i.e. "out of dislike that you return" (كَرَاهَةَ أَنْ تَعُودُوا), so it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
It is also said that the preposition was omitted, the verb being construed according to the meaning of يعظكم, i.e. "He restrains you from returning" (يَزْجُرُكُمْ عَنِ الْعَوْدِ).

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ وَمَنْ يَتَّبِعْ خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ فَإِنَّهُ يَأْمُرُ بِالْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ مَا زَكَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَدًا وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يُزَكِّي مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (٢١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِنَّهُ يَأْمُرُ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the devil (الشيطان), or the pronoun of مَن.
And (زَكَا) is pronounced with imāla (inclination of the alif towards yāʾ), by analogy with the inflection of the verb; and whoever does not use imāla says: the alif is from a wāw.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا يَأْتَلِ أُولُو الْفَضْلِ مِنْكُمْ وَالسَّعَةِ أَنْ يُؤْتُوا أُولِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْمَسَاكِينَ وَالْمُهَاجِرِينَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلْيَعْفُوا وَلْيَصْفَحُوا أَلَا تُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا يَأْتَلِ): it is of the pattern yaftaʿilu, from أَلَيْتُ, i.e. "I swore".
It is also read يَتَأَلَّ, on the pattern yatafaʿʿalu; it too is from الأَلِيَّة ("oath").

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَلْسِنَتُهُمْ وَأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ): the operator governing the adverb is the notion of settledness (istiqrār) in His saying, Exalted is He: (لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ); عذاب itself does not govern it, because it has been qualified by an adjective.
It is also said that the implied wording is: "mention" (اذْكُرْ).
And تشهد is read with yāʾ and with tāʾ, and that is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَوْمَئِذٍ يُوَفِّيهِمُ اللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ الْحَقَّ وَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ الْمُبِينُ (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَئِذٍ): the operator governing it is «يُوَفِّيهِمُ».
And (الْحَقَّ) in the accusative is an adjective of الدين; in the nominative it is an adjective of Allah, the separation being disregarded. Its parallel was mentioned in al-Kahf.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الْخَبِيثَاتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ وَالْخَبِيثُونَ لِلْخَبِيثَاتِ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ لِلطَّيِّبِينَ وَالطَّيِّبُونَ لِلطَّيِّبَاتِ أُولَئِكَ مُبَرَّءُونَ مِمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ (٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ): it may be resumptive, and it may be a khabar (predicate) after a khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ مَسْكُونَةٍ فِيهَا مَتَاعٌ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا تَكْتُمُونَ (٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا), i.e. "in that you enter" (فِي أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا). This has already been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُوا فُرُوجَهُمْ ذَلِكَ أَزْكَى لَهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا يَصْنَعُونَ (٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ): «مِنْ» here denotes the partitive, i.e. he is not required to lower his gaze entirely. It is also said that it is redundant (zāʾida). It is also said that it is for explaining the genus. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقُلْ لِلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِنَّ وَيَحْفَظْنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَلْيَضْرِبْنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَى جُيُوبِهِنَّ وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ آبَائِهِنَّ أَوْ آبَاءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ أَبْنَائِهِنَّ أَوْ أَبْنَاءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ إِخْوَانِهِنَّ أَوْ بَنِي إِخْوَانِهِنَّ أَوْ بَنِي أَخَوَاتِهِنَّ أَوْ نِسَائِهِنَّ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُنَّ أَوِ التَّابِعِينَ غَيْرِ أُولِي الْإِرْبَةِ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ أَوِ الطِّفْلِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلَى عَوْرَاتِ النِّسَاءِ وَلَا يَضْرِبْنَ بِأَرْجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعْلَمَ مَا يُخْفِينَ مِنْ زِينَتِهِنَّ وَتُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (غَيْرِ أُولِي الْإِرْبَةِ): in the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) or a badal (substitute); and in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) or as an exception. This was mentioned in al-Fātiḥa.
And (مِنَ الرِّجَالِ) is in the accusative as a ḥāl. The singular form of «الطِّفْلِ» was mentioned in al-Ḥajj.
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ زِينَتِهِنَّ): a ḥāl.
(أَيُّهَا): the majority give the hāʾ a fatḥa in continuous recitation, because there is an alif after it in the underlying form.
It has also been read with ḍamma on the hāʾ, in harmony with the ḍamma before it in pronunciation; this is far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلْيَسْتَعْفِفِ الَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا حَتَّى يُغْنِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَالَّذِينَ يَبْتَغُونَ الْكِتَابَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا وَآتُوهُمْ مِنْ مَالِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي آتَاكُمْ وَلَا تُكْرِهُوا فَتَيَاتِكُمْ عَلَى الْبِغَاءِ إِنْ أَرَدْنَ تَحَصُّنًا لِتَبْتَغُوا عَرَضَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَنْ يُكْرِهُّنَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ يَبْتَغُونَ): nominative or accusative, as was mentioned at (الَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ), i.e. "forgiving", that is, towards them (the women).

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (اللَّهُ نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ مَثَلُ نُورِهِ كَمِشْكَاةٍ فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ الْمِصْبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍ الزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّيٌّ يُوقَدُ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ مُبَارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ لَا شَرْقِيَّةٍ وَلَا غَرْبِيَّةٍ يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا يُضِيءُ وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ نُورٌ عَلَى نُورٍ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ لِنُورِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اللَّهُ نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ): its implied wording is: "the Possessor of the light of the heavens" (صَاحِبُ نُورِ السَّمَاوَاتِ). It is also said that the maṣdar (verbal noun) has the sense of the active participle, i.e. "the Illuminator of the heavens" (مُنَوِّرُ السَّمَاوَاتِ).
(فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ): an adjective of مشكاة.
His saying, Exalted is He: (دُرِّيٌّ): it is read with ḍamma and doubling, without hamza; it is a relative adjective (nisba) from الدُّرّ ("pearls"), the star being likened to it for its clarity and its brightness.
It is also possible that its origin is with hamza, but the hamza was lightened and assimilated; it is then of the pattern fuʿʿīl from الدَّرْء, which is the repelling of darkness by its light.
It is also read with kasra, in the sense of the second view, being then of the pattern fiʿʿīl, like سِكِّيت and صِدِّيق.
It is also read with fatḥa, on the pattern faʿʿīl; this is far-fetched. (تَوَقَّدَ): with tāʾ and fatḥa, as a past verb; and تُوقَدُ as an imperfect verb; the tāʾ is for the feminine of الزجاجة, and the yāʾ is according to the meaning of المصباح. And (زَيْتُونَةٍ) is a badal (substitute) of شجرة. And (لَا شَرْقِيَّةٍ) is a naʿt (adjective). (يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا): the clause is a naʿt of زيتونة. (نُورٌ عَلَى نُورٍ), i.e. "that is light upon light" (ذَلِكَ نُورٌ).

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فِي بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ اللَّهُ أَنْ تُرْفَعَ وَيُذْكَرَ فِيهَا اسْمُهُ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ رِجَالٌ لَا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَارَةٌ وَلَا بَيْعٌ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَإِقَامِ الصَّلَاةِ وَإِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ يَخَافُونَ يَوْمًا تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ الْقُلُوبُ وَالْأَبْصَارُ (٣٧)). [Translator's note: the verse quoted here combines verses 36 and 37.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي بُيُوتٍ): concerning what it is attached to there are several views:
The first: it is an adjective of زجاجة in His saying: (الْمِصْبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍ), i.e. "in houses". The second: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to توقد, i.e. "it is found in the mosques".
The third: it is attached to يسبح, and the «فِيهَا» after «يُسَبِّحُ» is a repetition, like His saying: (وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ سُعِدُوا فَفِي الْجَنَّةِ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا). It cannot be attached to يذكر, because that is conjoined to «تُرْفَعَ» and is inside the ṣila of «أَنْ», so it cannot govern anything before it.
And (يُسَبِّحُ) is read with kasra on the bāʾ, the fāʿil (agent) being (رِجَالٌ); and with fatḥa, with the element standing in place of the agent being له or فيها. رجال is then nominative by an omitted verb, as though it were asked: "Who glorifies Him?" and He said: "Men", i.e. "men glorify Him" (يُسَبِّحُهُ رِجَالٌ). It is also said that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the glorifiers are men" (الْمُسَبِّحُ رِجَالٌ). It is also said that the implied wording is: "in them are men" (فِيهَا رِجَالٌ).
(وَإِقَامِ الصَّلَاةِ): this was mentioned in al-Anbiyāʾ; i.e. "and from establishing the prayer" (وَعَنْ إِقَامِ الصَّلَاةِ).
(يَخَافُونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «تُلْهِيهِمْ», and it may be a further adjective of رجال.

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لِيَجْزِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنَ مَا عَمِلُوا وَيَزِيدَهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَاللَّهُ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِيَجْزِيَهُمْ): the lām may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to يسبح, to «لَا تُلْهِيهِمْ», or to يخافون.
It may also be the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra), like the one in His saying: (لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا), and its position is that of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the implied wording is: "they fear, being distracted, so that He may reward them" (يَخَافُونَ مُلْهِينَ لِيَجْزِيَهُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَعْمَالُهُمْ كَسَرَابٍ بِقِيعَةٍ يَحْسَبُهُ الظَّمْآنُ مَاءً حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَهُ لَمْ يَجِدْهُ شَيْئًا وَوَجَدَ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ فَوَفَّاهُ حِسَابَهُ وَاللَّهُ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ (٣٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِقِيعَةٍ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective of سراب.
It may also be an adverb, the operator governing it being what the kāf, which is the khabar (predicate), is attached to.
The yāʾ in «قِيعَةٍ» replaces a wāw, because of its being vowelless and the kasra before it; for they said, for قاع, the plural أقواع.
It is also read قِيعَاتٍ, which is the plural of قيعة; and the alif may be additional, like the alif of سِعْلاة, so that it is a singular. And (يَحْسَبُهُ) is also an adjective of سراب. And (شَيْئًا) is in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "he did not find it in any finding at all" (لَمْ يَجِدْهُ وُجْدَانًا); it is also said that «شَيْئًا» here means "water", in accordance with what he supposed. (وَوَجَدَ اللَّهَ), i.e. "the decree of Allah", or "Allah's causing death".

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍّ يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ سَحَابٌ ظُلُمَاتٌ بَعْضُهَا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ إِذَا أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا وَمَنْ لَمْ يَجْعَلِ اللَّهُ لَهُ نُورًا فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ نُورٍ (٤٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ): it is conjoined to «كَسَرَابٍ», and concerning the implied wording there are two views:
The first: its implied wording is "or like the deeds of one in darknesses" (أَوْ كَأَعْمَالِ ذِي ظُلُمَاتٍ); «ذِي» is supplied so that the pronoun in His saying «إِذَا أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ» may refer back to it, and "deeds" is supplied so that the comparison of the deeds of the unbelievers to the deeds of the one in darkness may be sound, since there is no sense in comparing deeds to the one in darknesses. The second: there is no omission in it; the meaning is that He compared the deeds of the unbelievers to darkness in its coming between the heart and what it would be guided to. As for the pronoun in His saying (إِذَا أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ), it refers to something mentioned implicitly and omitted in reliance on the meaning; its implied wording is: "when whoever is in it puts out his hand" (إِذَا أَخْرَجَ مَنْ فِيهَا يَدَهُ).
(فِي بَحْرٍ): an adjective of ظلمات.
And (لُجِّيٍّ) is a relative adjective (nisba) from اللُّجّ ("the deep sea"), and it means "having a vast deep" (ذِي لُجَّةٍ). And (يَغْشَاهُ) is a further adjective.
And (مِنْ فَوْقِهِ) is an adjective of موج. The second موج is nominative by the adverbial phrase, because it is supported (by what precedes it).
It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), the adverbial phrase being its khabar (predicate). And (مِنْ فَوْقِهِ سَحَابٌ) is a naʿt (adjective) of the second موج. And (ظُلُمَاتٌ) in the nominative is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "these are darknesses" (هَذِهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ).
It is also read سَحَابُ ظُلُمَاتٍ, with annexation and the genitive, treating the piled-up waves as being like clouds.
It is also read سَحَابٌ, nominative with nunation, and ظُلُمَاتٍ in the genitive, as a badal (substitute) of the first ظلمات.
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا): people have differed about the interpretation of this phrase; the origin of the disagreement is the function of «كَادَ» when you negate the occurrence of the verb. Most of the commentators hold that the meaning is that he does not see his hand; on this view there are three views of the implied wording. The first: the implied wording is "he did not see it, and he almost did not" (لَمْ يَرَهَا وَلَمْ يَكَدْ); a group of the grammarians mentioned it. This is a mistake, because the words "he did not see it" are a categorical negation of seeing, while His saying, Exalted is He: «لَمْ يَكَدْ», when it is taken out of what the chapter requires, gives the implied wording "and he almost did not see it" (وَلَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا), as is stated explicitly in the verse. So if this speaker means by "he almost did not see it" that he saw it after effort, he contradicts himself, because he negated the seeing and then affirmed it.
And if the meaning of "he almost did not see it" is that he did not see it at all, contrary to what holds most of the time in this chapter, then it ought to be construed that way without supplying "he did not see it".
The second view: that «كَادَ» is redundant (zāʾida); this is far-fetched.
The third: that كاد has been used here in the sense of "came near" (قَارَبَ). The meaning is: he did not come near to seeing it, and if he did not come near to it, he was far from it. In this sense comes the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
إِذَا غَيَّرَ النَّأْيُ الْمُحِبِّينَ لَمْ يَكَدْ ... رَسِيسُ الْهَوَى مِنْ حُبِّ مَيَّةَ يَبْرَحُ
(When distance changes lovers, the lingering touch of passion from love of Mayya hardly departs.)
i.e. it did not come near to departing. It is from this that it is reported of Dhū al-Rumma that he was challenged about this verse of poetry and said: "I did not find a substitute for لم يكد."
The second meaning: "he strove, and then saw it" [Translator's note: the Arabic reads «جَهَدَ أَنَّهُ رَآهَا بَعْدُ», apparently for «جَهْدًا أَنَّهُ رَآهَا بَعْدُ» or similar; translated according to the evident sense: that he saw it only after effort]; on this view the comparison is sound, because even with the intensity of the darkness, if he sharpened his gaze towards his hand and brought it near to his eye, he would see it.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَالطَّيْرُ صَافَّاتٍ كُلٌّ قَدْ عَلِمَ صَلَاتَهُ وَتَسْبِيحَهُ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِمَا يَفْعَلُونَ (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالطَّيْرُ): it is conjoined to «مَنْ», and «صَافَّاتٍ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الطير.
(كُلٌّ قَدْ عَلِمَ صَلَاتَهُ): the agent pronoun in علم is the name of Allah according to some, and according to others it is the pronoun of كل; this is the stronger view, because the reading has كل in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), so the agent pronoun refers back to it. Had it contained the pronoun of the name of Allah, it would have been preferable to put كل in the accusative, because the verb after it has made accusative something connected with it; it would then be like your saying: "Zayd, ʿAmr struck his servant" (زَيْدًا ضَرَبَ عَمْرٌو غُلَامَهُ), where you make Zayd accusative by a verb indicated by what follows it; and that is stronger than the nominative, though the other is permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُزْجِي سَحَابًا ثُمَّ يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُ ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ رُكَامًا فَتَرَى الْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلَالِهِ وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِنْ جِبَالٍ فِيهَا مِنْ بَرَدٍ فَيُصِيبُ بِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَصْرِفُهُ عَنْ مَنْ يَشَاءُ يَكَادُ سَنَا بَرْقِهِ يَذْهَبُ بِالْأَبْصَارِ (٤٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُ): بين is allowed to come before a singular here only because the meaning is "between each piece and piece"; [each piece is] a سحابة, and السحاب is the collective (genus) noun for it.
(وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ): (مِنَ) here is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). As for (مِنْ جِبَالٍ), there are two views on (مِنْ):
The first: it is redundant (zāʾida); this is according to the opinion of al-Akhfash. The second: it is not redundant. Then there are two views on it. The first: it is a badal (substitute) of the first one, with the preposition repeated; the implied wording is "and He sends down from the mountains of the sky", i.e. from mountains in the sky; on this view «مِنْ بَرَدٍ» is redundant according to some and not redundant according to others. The second view: the implied wording is "something from mountains" (شَيْئًا مِنْ جِبَالٍ); the qualified noun was omitted and the adjective sufficed.
This view is the correct one, because His saying, Exalted is He: «فِيهَا مِنْ بَرَدٍ» requires you to have an object to which the pronoun refers; the implied wording [on the other view] would be: "and He sends down from the mountains of the sky mountains in which there is hail", and that involves extra omission and supplying something that is not needed.
As for the second «مِنْ», there are two views on it. The first: it is redundant. The second: it is partitive.

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلَى بَطْنِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلَى رِجْلَيْنِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلَى أَرْبَعٍ يَخْلُقُ اللَّهُ مَا يَشَاءُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلَى بَطْنِهِ) and (مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلَى أَرْبَعٍ): «مَنْ» in both is used for what is not rational, because it accompanies a مَن used for the rational, so it was better for their wording to agree. It is also said: since He described these two with walking and choice, He treated them as rational beings.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا دُعُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِذَا فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ (٤٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذَا فَرِيقٌ): it is the إذا of surprise (al-mufājaʾa); it has been mentioned before in several places.

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّمَا كَانَ قَوْلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذَا دُعُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ أَنْ يَقُولُوا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ (٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَوْلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): it is read in the accusative and in the nominative; its parallel has been mentioned in several places.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَخْشَ اللَّهَ وَيَتَّقْهِ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَائِزُونَ (٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَتَّقْهِ): this was mentioned at His saying, Exalted is He: (يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ).

ukberi-tibyan:53-54.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ لَئِنْ أَمَرْتَهُمْ لَيَخْرُجُنَّ قُلْ لَا تُقْسِمُوا طَاعَةٌ مَعْرُوفَةٌ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ (٥٣) قُلْ أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْهِ مَا حُمِّلَ وَعَلَيْكُمْ مَا حُمِّلْتُمْ وَإِنْ تُطِيعُوهُ تَهْتَدُوا وَمَا عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ الْمُبِينُ (٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (طَاعَةٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "is better than anything else" (أَمْثَلُ مِنْ غَيْرِهَا). It may also be a khabar with the mubtadaʾ omitted, i.e. "our command is obedience" (أَمْرُنَا طَاعَةٌ).
Had it been read in the accusative, it would have been permissible in Arabic, as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "obey with an obedience, and say a saying" (أَطِيعُوا طَاعَةً، وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا), or "adopt obedience and a saying" (اتَّخِذُوا طَاعَةً وَقَوْلًا); His saying after it, Exalted is He: «قُلْ أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ», indicates this.

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ كَمَا اسْتَخْلَفَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ لَهُمْ دِينَهُمُ الَّذِي ارْتَضَى لَهُمْ وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ خَوْفِهِمْ أَمْنًا يَعْبُدُونَنِي لَا يُشْرِكُونَ بِي شَيْئًا وَمَنْ كَفَرَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ (٥٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَمَا اسْتَخْلَفَ): a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a succession like the one He made" (اسْتِخْلَافًا كَمَا اسْتَخْلَفَ).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَعْبُدُونَنِي): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in «لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ», or from the pronoun in «لَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ». [Translator's note: so in the source; the pronoun that the ḥāl refers to here is presumably the object pronoun هم in these verbs.]
(لَا يُشْرِكُونَ): it may be a ḥāl serving as a badal (substitute) of the first ḥāl, and it may be a ḥāl from the agent in «يَعْبُدُونَنِي», i.e. "they worship Me, professing My oneness" (يَعْبُدُونَنِي مُوَحِّدِينَ).

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مُعْجِزِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَأْوَاهُمُ النَّارُ وَلَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ (٥٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ): it is read with yāʾ and with tāʾ; the like of this was mentioned in al-Anfāl.

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِيَسْتَأْذِنْكُمُ الَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا الْحُلُمَ مِنْكُمْ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ ثِيَابَكُمْ مِنَ الظَّهِيرَةِ وَمِنْ بَعْدِ صَلَاةِ الْعِشَاءِ ثَلَاثُ عَوْرَاتٍ لَكُمْ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَا عَلَيْهِمْ جُنَاحٌ بَعْدَهُنَّ طَوَّافُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ بَعْضُكُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ وَإِذَا بَلَغَ الْأَطْفَالُ مِنْكُمُ الْحُلُمَ فَلْيَسْتَأْذِنُوا كَمَا اسْتَأْذَنَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آيَاتِهِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ (٥٨)). [Translator's note: the quotation here combines verses 58 and 59.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ): مرّة is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), but it has come to be used as an adverb; on this basis «ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ» is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and the operator is ليستأذن. On this basis there are three views on the position of «مِنْ قَبْلِ صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ». The first: accusative, as a badal (substitute) of ثلاث. The second: genitive, as a badal of مرّات. The third: nominative, as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are: before…" (هِيَ مِنْ قَبْلِ), and the rest of the three is conjoined to this.
(مِنَ الظَّهِيرَةِ): من may be for explaining the genus, i.e. "at that time, out of the time of midday"; it may be in the sense of في ("in"); and it may be in the sense of "on account of the heat of midday" (مِنْ أَجْلِ حَرِّ الظَّهِيرَةِ).
And (حِينَ) is conjoined to the position of «مِنْ قَبْلِ».
His saying, Exalted is He: (ثَلَاثُ عَوْرَاتٍ): it is read in the nominative, i.e. "they are the times of three occasions of exposure" (هِيَ أَوْقَاتُ ثَلَاثِ عَوْرَاتٍ); the mubtadaʾ and the muḍāf were omitted.
And in the accusative, as a badal of the times mentioned, or of the first «ثَلَاثَ», or by an implied "I mean" (أَعْنِي).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَعْدَهُنَّ): the implied wording is "after their asking permission during them" (بَعْدَ اسْتِئْذَانِهِنَّ فِيهِنَّ); then the preposition and the agent were omitted, leaving "after asking permission for it" (بَعْدَ اسْتِئْذَانِهِ), and then the maṣdar was omitted.
His saying, Exalted is He: (طَوَّافُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ), i.e. "they are ones who go about" (هُمْ طَوَّافُونَ).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَعْضُكُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ), i.e. "some of you go about among others" (بَعْضُكُمْ يَطُوفُ عَلَى بَعْضٍ); so the clause may be a badal of the one before it, and it may be explanatory and emphatic. [Translator's note: the Arabic reads «مَبْنِيَّةً مُؤَكِّدَةً», apparently for «مُبَيِّنَةً مُؤَكِّدَةً»; translated according to the evident sense.]

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالْقَوَاعِدُ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ اللَّاتِي لَا يَرْجُونَ نِكَاحًا فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِنَّ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ يَضَعْنَ ثِيَابَهُنَّ غَيْرَ مُتَبَرِّجَاتٍ بِزِينَةٍ وَأَنْ يَسْتَعْفِفْنَ خَيْرٌ لَهُنَّ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (٦٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْقَوَاعِدُ): the singular is قاعد, this being when she is old, i.e. one who has ceased from (sitting back from) marriage. And from القعود ("sitting") the form is قاعدة, to distinguish between masculine and feminine. It is a mubtadaʾ (subject).
And (مِنَ النِّسَاءِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «اللَّاتِي» is an adjective. The khabar (predicate) is «فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِنَّ»; the fāʾ came in because of the conditional sense in the mubtadaʾ, since the alif and lām (the definite article) are in the sense of الذي.
(غَيْرَ): a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَيْسَ عَلَى الْأَعْمَى حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَى الْأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَى الْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَنْ تَأْكُلُوا مِنْ بُيُوتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ آبَائِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ إِخْوَانِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَخَوَاتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَعْمَامِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ عَمَّاتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَخْوَالِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ خَالَاتِكُمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكْتُمْ مَفَاتِحَهُ أَوْ صَدِيقِكُمْ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَأْكُلُوا جَمِيعًا أَوْ أَشْتَاتًا فَإِذَا دَخَلْتُمْ بُيُوتًا فَسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ تَحِيَّةً مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ مُبَارَكَةً طَيِّبَةً كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ (٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوْ مَا مَلَكْتُمْ): the majority read it without doubling. It is also read «مُلِّكْتُمْ» with doubling, in the passive.
And المفاتح is the plural of مِفْتَح; it is said that this is the very thing with which something is opened.
It is also said that it is the plural of مَفْتَح, which is the maṣdar (verbal noun), like الفتح ("opening").
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَحِيَّةً): a maṣdar derived from the meaning of سلّموا, because سلّم ("to greet with peace") and حيّا ("to greet") have the same meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَا تَجْعَلُوا دُعَاءَ الرَّسُولِ بَيْنَكُمْ كَدُعَاءِ بَعْضِكُمْ بَعْضًا قَدْ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ يَتَسَلَّلُونَ مِنْكُمْ لِوَاذًا فَلْيَحْذَرِ الَّذِينَ يُخَالِفُونَ عَنْ أَمْرِهِ أَنْ تُصِيبَهُمْ فِتْنَةٌ أَوْ يُصِيبَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (دُعَاءَ الرَّسُولِ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its object, i.e. "your calling the Messenger" (دُعَاءَكُمُ الرَّسُولَ). It may also be annexed to its agent, i.e. "do not neglect his calling you" (لَا تُهْمِلُوا دُعَاءَهُ إِيَّاكُمْ).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِوَاذًا): it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). It may also be accusative by يتسللون according to the meaning, i.e. "they seek cover, a seeking of cover" (يُلَاوِذُونَ لِوَاذًا), or "they slip away, a slipping away" (يَتَسَلَّلُونَ تَسَلُّلًا). The wāw in «لِوَاذًا» remained sound despite the kasra before it only because it is sound in the verb, which is لَاوَذَ; had it been the maṣdar of لَاذَ, it would have been لِيَاذًا, like صَامَ صِيَامًا.
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَنْ أَمْرِهِ): the expression is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning of يخالفون is "they turn aside and deviate".
(أَنْ تُصِيبَهُمْ) is the object of يحذر. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Nūr
Medinan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سُورَةٌ أنْـزَلْناها﴾ — the reading is with the nominative (rafʿ), and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read "سُورَةً" in the accusative (naṣb). As for the nominative, it is by an implied "هَذِهِ سُورَةٌ أنْزَلْناها" (this is a sūra which We have sent down); making it nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) is ugly, because it is indefinite, and "أنْزَلْناها" is a ṣifa (adjective) of it. The accusative is on two possibilities: with the meaning "أنْزَلْنا سُورَةً" (We sent down a sūra), just as you say "زَيْدًا ضَرَبْتُهُ" (Zayd, I struck him), and with the meaning "اُتْلُ سُورَةً أنْزَلْناها" (recite a sūra which We have sent down). ﴿وَفَرَضْناها﴾ is with the rāʾ unstressed, and it is also read with the rāʾ doubled (فَرَّضْناها). Whoever reads it unstressed, its meaning is "ألْزَمْناكُمُ العَمَلَ بِما فُرِضَ فِيها" (We have bound you to act upon what is ordained in it). Whoever reads it doubled, it is on two possibilities: one of them in the sense of multiplicity, meaning "إنّا فَرَضْنا فِيها فُرُوضًا كَثِيرَةً" (We have ordained many ordinances in it), and [the other] in the sense of "بَيَّنّا، وفَصَّلْنا" (We have made clear and set out in detail) what is in it of the lawful and the unlawful.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿الزّانِيَةُ والزّانِي فاجْلِدُوا كُلَّ واحِدٍ مِنهُما مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ﴾ — the reading is with the nominative (rafʿ), and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it in the accusative (naṣb): "اَلزّانِيَةَ والزّانِيَ", with fatḥa on the tāʾ. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh claimed that the accusative is the preferred [form], and Sībawayh claimed that the reading is the nominative; others among the Basrans and the Kufans claimed that the preferred [form] is the nominative, and so it is in my view, because the nominative is as if by consensus in the reading, and it is stronger in Arabic, since its meaning is the meaning of "مَن زَنى فاجْلِدُوهُ" (whoever commits fornication, flog him), so its interpretation is as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Sībawayh and al-Khalīl said that the nominative is in the sense of "وَفِيما فَرَضْنا عَلَيْكُمُ الزّانِيَةُ والزّانِي" (and among what We have ordained for you: the fornicatress and the fornicator), in the nominative, or "اَلزّانِيَةُ والزّانِي فِيما فُرِضَ عَلَيْكم" (the fornicatress and the fornicator, in what is ordained for you). The proof that the preferred [form] is the nominative is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واللَّذانِ يَأْتِيانِها مِنكم فَآذُوهُما﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 16]. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh only preferred the accusative because it is a command, and a command is more fitting with a verb. The accusative is permissible in the sense of "اِجْلِدُوا الزّانِيَةَ والزّانِيَ" (flog the fornicatress and the fornicator). The consensus is that flogging applies to those who are not muḥṣan (not married and chaste): the unmarried man and the unmarried woman are flogged one hundred lashes, and banishment goes together with the flogging in the view of many jurists: "he is flogged one hundred and exiled for a year"; as for the people of Iraq, they flog him one hundred.
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَأْخُذْكم بِهِما رَأْفَةٌ في دِينِ اللَّهِ﴾ — it is also read "رَآفَةٌ في دِينِ اللَّهِ", on the pattern of "رَعافَةٌ", and it is read "يَأْخُذْكم" with the yāʾ. "رَآفَةٌ" is like "اَلسَّآمَةُ", as in your saying "سَئِمْتُ سَآمَةً" (I grew weary, weariness), and like it is "كَآبَةٌ"; for "فَعالَةٌ" is among the noun-patterns of maṣdars (verbal nouns), and "سَآمَةٌ" is on the analogy of "كَلالَةٌ"; and "فَعالَةٌ" is used for qualities, such as "اَلْقَباحَةُ" (ugliness), "اَلْمَلاحَةُ" (comeliness) and "اَلْفَخامَةُ" (grandeur), and this is very frequent. The meaning of ﴿وَلا تَأْخُذْكم بِهِما رَأْفَةٌ في دِينِ اللَّهِ﴾ is: "do not have mercy on them so that you drop from them the ḥadd (prescribed punishment) that Allah has commanded"; and it was said: "[it means that] they are flogged severely". His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذابَهُما طائِفَةٌ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — the reading is with sukūn on the lām, and kasra on it is permissible. People differed about "الطّائِفَةُ" (a party): some of them said: one and above is a "طائِفَةٌ"; others said: a ṭāʾifa is not less than two; some of them said: three; some said: four; and some said: ten. As for whoever said "one", that is contrary to what the people of the language hold, because "اَلطّائِفَةُ" has the meaning of "اَلْجَماعَةُ" (a group), and the least of a group is two. The least that is required for a ṭāʾifa, in my view, is two, and what ought to be sought in witnessing the punishment of the fornicator is that they be a group, because what predominates in [the meaning of] ṭāʾifa is "اَلْجَماعَةُ" (a group).

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿الزّانِي لا يَنْكِحُ إلا زانِيَةً أوْ مُشْرِكَةً والزّانِيَةُ لا يَنْكِحُها إلا زانٍ أوْ مُشْرِكٌ﴾ — it is permissible to say "اَلزّانِي لا يُنْكَحُ إلّا زانِيَةً" and "اَلزّانِيَةُ لا يُنْكَحُها إلّا زانٍ", but it has not been read thus. [Translator's note: the forms are given as written in the source.] The interpretation of "اَلزّانِي لا يَنْكِحُ إلّا زانِيَةً" is in the sense of "لا يَتَزَوَّجُ" (he does not marry), and likewise "اَلزّانِيَةُ لا يَتَزَوَّجُها إلّا زانٍ" (none marries the fornicatress except a fornicator). Some people said that the meaning of nikāḥ here is intercourse, so the meaning according to them is: "the fornicator has intercourse only with a fornicatress, and none has intercourse with the fornicatress except a fornicator". This view is far-fetched, because nothing is known of the mention of nikāḥ in the Book of Allah except in the sense of marriage. Allah, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَأنْكِحُوا الأيامى مِنكم والصّالِحِينَ مِن عِبادِكم وإمائِكُمْ﴾ [al-Nūr: 32], and this is marriage without any doubt; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا نَكَحْتُمُ المُؤْمِناتِ ثُمَّ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 49], so He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the contract of marriage is called "اَلنِّكاحُ". Most of the exegesis holds that this verse was revealed concerning some poor Muslims who were in Medina and who intended to marry prostitutes who were in Medina, who committed fornication and took payment; they wanted to marry them so that the women would support them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down the prohibition of that. It was also said that they wanted to be indulgent with them, and they were informed that this is forbidden.
It is related that al-Ḥasan said: the fornicator, when the ḥadd (prescribed punishment) has been carried out on him, is married only to a woman on whom the ḥadd has been carried out like him; and likewise the woman, when the ḥadd has been carried out on her, according to him, is married only to a man like her. Some of them said: the verse is abrogated; it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿وَأنْكِحُوا الأيامى مِنكُمْ﴾ [al-Nūr: 32]. Most of the opinion is that the meaning here is marriage. It is permissible to say "وَحَرَّمَ ذَلِكَ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ" (and He forbade that to the believers), in the sense of "وَحَرَّمَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ" (and Allah forbade that to the believers), but it has not been read thus. This is a statement in wording, but its meaning is that of a command. Had it been as those who said it is intercourse claimed, there would be no benefit in the speech, because if the speaker says: the fornicatress fornicates only with a fornicator, and the fornicator fornicates only with a fornicatress, there is no benefit in it except by way of intensifying the matter, as you say of a man whom you have known for lying: "هَذا كَذّابٌ" (this one is a liar), intending to make his case grave. So according to what carries benefit, and what the language requires, the meaning is that of marriage.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم ورَحْمَتُهُ وأنَّ اللَّهَ تَوّابٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ — here the answer (jawāb) of "لَوْلا" is left out, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم لَنالَ الكاذِبُ لِما ذَكَرْنا عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ" (were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you, a great punishment would have befallen the liar for what We mentioned), and this is indicated by: ﴿وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم ورَحْمَتُهُ في الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ لَمَسَّكم في ما أفَضْتُمْ فِيهِ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ [al-Nūr: 14].

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ جاءُوا بِالإفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِنكُمْ﴾ — the meaning of "اَلْإفْكُ" here is the lie. Some of them have been named in the reports (āthār), but they were not named in the Qurʾān. Among those named are Ḥassān ibn Thābit, Misṭaḥ ibn Uthātha and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, and among the women Ḥamna bint Jaḥsh. ﴿لا تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرًّا لَكم بَلْ هو خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ — it said "لَكم" (for you, plural), while the one who was targeted was ʿĀʾisha, may Allah have mercy on her; so it was said "لَكم", by which is meant: she and those connected with her, namely the Prophet ﷺ and Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him.
His saying: ﴿والَّذِي تَوَلّى كِبْرَهُ مِنهُمْ﴾, and it is also read "كُبْرَهُ مِنهم", ﴿لَهُ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾. Whoever reads "كِبْرَهُ", its meaning is: whoever took upon himself the sin in that; and whoever reads "كُبْرَهُ" means: the greater part of it. It is related that Ḥassān ibn Thābit came in to ʿĀʾisha, and it was said to her: Do you let in this man about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿والَّذِي تَوَلّى كِبْرَهُ مِنهم لَهُ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾? She said: "Has not his sight gone?" And it is related that he recited to her his saying in his verse:
؎حَصانٌ رَزانٌ ما تُزَنُّ بِرِيبَةٍ ∗∗∗ وتُصْبِحُ غَرْثى مِن لُحُومِ الغَوافِلِ
(Chaste, composed, never suspected of any doubt; she wakes hungry of the flesh of unwary women — i.e. she does not backbite them.)
She said to him: "But you are not like that." And His saying, Exalted is He: "والخامِسَةُ أنْ غَضَبُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها", with "أنَّ" lightened and "غَضَبُ" in the nominative, in the sense of "أنَّهُ غَضَبُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها" (that it is: the wrath of Allah be upon her); and it is permissible to say "أنْ غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْها" (that Allah is wroth with her). Here there is an implied (muḍmar) "hāʾ", and "أنْ" is lightened from the heavy one; the meaning is "أنَّهُ غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْها" and "أنَّهُ غَضَبُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها". [Translator's note: this discussion concerns al-Nūr: 9 and is placed here in the source.] The poet said:
؎فِي فِتْيَةٍ كَسُيُوفِ الهِنْدِ قَدْ عَلِمُوا ∗∗∗ أنْ هالِكٌ كُلُّ مَن يَحْفى ويَنْتَعِلُ
(Among young men like Indian swords, who knew that everyone who goes barefoot or shod will perish.)
It came in the exegesis concerning His saying ﴿لا تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرًّا لَكم بَلْ هو خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ that by it are meant ʿĀʾisha and Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal; and "لَكم" may be in the sense of "لَكُما" (for you two). What we explained first includes the matter of ʿĀʾisha, Ṣafwān, the Prophet ﷺ, and everyone who had a connection with ʿĀʾisha; and it may be for everyone who was accused on account of [this matter].

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لَوْلا إذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ المُؤْمِنُونَ والمُؤْمِناتُ بِأنْفُسِهِمْ خَيْرًا﴾ — its meaning is: "هَلّا إذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ؟" (why, when you heard it, did not…?), because the meaning of "ظَنَّ المُؤْمِنُونَ بِأنْفُسِهِمْ" is in place of an allusion to them and to some of them; and likewise it is said of people some of whom kill others: "إنَّهم يَقْتُلُونَ أنْفُسَهم" (they kill themselves). ﴿وَقالُوا هَذا إفْكٌ مُبِينٌ﴾, that is: a manifest lie.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ المُحْصَناتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِأرْبَعَةِ شُهَداءَ فاجْلِدُوهم ثَمانِينَ جَلْدَةً﴾ — the meaning of "يَرْمُونَ المُحْصَناتِ" is: [accuse them] of fornication; but He did not say "بِالزِّنا" (of fornication), because in the preceding mention of the fornicatress and the fornicator there is an indication that this is the meaning. The position of "اَلَّذِينَ" is nominative (rafʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject). On the reading of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, the position of "اَلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ المُحْصَناتِ" must be accusative (naṣb), in the sense of "اِجْلِدُوا الَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ المُحْصَناتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِأرْبَعَةِ شُهَداءَ" (flog those who accuse chaste women and then do not bring four witnesses), and on that is the preference of Sībawayh and al-Khalīl. "اَلْمُحْصَناتُ" here are the women who have guarded their private parts through chastity.
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْبَلُوا لَهم شَهادَةً أبَدًا وأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾ ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وأصْلَحُوا﴾ [al-Nūr: 5] — people differed about accepting the testimony of the slanderer (al-qādhif). Some of them said: if he repents of his slander, his testimony is accepted; and it is related that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb accepted the testimony of two slanderers, and said to Abū Bakra: "If you repent, I will accept your testimony"; and his repentance is that he retract the slander. This is the position of most jurists. As for the people of Iraq, they say: his testimony is not accepted, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وَلا تَقْبَلُوا لَهم شَهادَةً أبَدًا﴾. They said: and His saying ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وأصْلَحُوا فَإنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [al-Nūr: 5] — they said: this exception is from His saying ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾, so those who repent are excepted from the transgressors. Those who claimed that his testimony is accepted said: the exception is from His saying ﴿وَلا تَقْبَلُوا لَهم شَهادَةً أبَدًا﴾ — ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا﴾ [al-Nūr: 5]; they said: and His saying ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾ is a description of them. They agreed by consensus that whoever slandered while a disbeliever, then embraced Islam and repented, and was upright after his Islam, his testimony is accepted, even though he was a slanderer. Analogy requires accepting the testimony of the slanderer if he repents; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says regarding testimonies: ﴿مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ الشُّهَداءِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 282], and the slanderer is not graver in crime than the disbeliever, so it is his due that, if he repents and makes amends, his testimony be accepted, just as the disbeliever, if he embraces Islam and makes amends, has his testimony accepted.
If someone says: then what is the benefit of His saying "أبَدًا" (ever)? It is said: the benefit is that "ever" for every person is the extent of his span in his life, and the extent of his span in what is connected with his case. So you say: "اَلْكافِرُ لا يُقْبَلُ مِنهُ شَيْءٌ أبَدًا" (nothing is ever accepted from the disbeliever), and its meaning is: "as long as he remains a disbeliever, nothing is accepted from him". Likewise when you say: "اَلْقاذِفُ لا تُقْبَلُ مِنهُ شَهادَةٌ أبَدًا" (no testimony is ever accepted from the slanderer), its meaning is: "as long as he remains a slanderer". So when disbelief departs from him, his "ever" has departed; and likewise the slanderer, when the slander departs from him, his "ever" has departed from him, and there is no difference between this and that. It is also read: "ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِأرْبَعَةٍ شُهَداءَ", with tanwīn, ﴿فاجْلِدُوهُمْ﴾; so "أرْبَعَةٍ" is genitive (makhfūḍ) with tanwīn, and "شُهَداءَ" is a ṣifa (adjective) of "أرْبَعَة", in the position of the genitive (jarr). It may also be in the position of the accusative (naṣb) from two angles: one of them in the sense of "ثُمَّ لَمْ يُحْضِرُوا أرْبَعَةً شُهَداءَ" (then they did not bring forward four witnesses), and [the other] as the accusative of ḥāl (circumstantial) with an indefinite: then they did not come in the state of [being] witnesses. As for ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا﴾ [al-Nūr: 5], it may be in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ and mīm (in «لَهُمْ»), in the sense of "وَلا تَقْبَلُوا لَهم شَهادَةً أبَدًا إلّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا" (and do not ever accept testimony from them, except those who repent); and it may be in the position of the accusative as an exception, upon His saying ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾ ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا﴾ [al-Nūr: 5]. And if they are excepted from the transgressors as well, then acceptance of their testimony becomes obligatory, because the name of transgression has departed from them.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أزْواجَهم ولَمْ يَكُنْ لَهم شُهَداءُ إلا أنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: "والَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أزْواجَهم بِالزِّنا" (and those who accuse their wives of fornication).
His saying: ﴿فَشَهادَةُ أحَدِهِمْ أرْبَعُ شَهاداتٍ بِاللَّهِ﴾ — it is also read "أرْبَعَ شَهاداتٍ بِاللَّهِ" in the accusative (naṣb). Whoever reads "أرْبَعُ" in the nominative (rafʿ), it is as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject); the meaning is: "the testimony of one of them which wards off the ḥadd of the slanderer is four", and the proof of that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَدْرَأُ عَنْها العَذابَ أنْ تَشْهَدَ أرْبَعَ شَهاداتٍ بِاللَّهِ﴾ [al-Nūr: 8]. Whoever puts "أرْبَعًا" in the accusative, the meaning is: "فَعَلَيْهِمْ أنْ يَشْهَدَ أحَدُهم أرْبَعَ شَهاداتٍ" (it is upon them that one of them testify four testimonies), and in the sense of "فالَّذِي يَدْرَأُ عَنْها العَذابَ أنْ يَشْهَدَ أحَدُهم أرْبَعَ شَهاداتٍ" (what wards off the punishment from her is that one of them testify four testimonies). [Translator's note: the source has «عَنْها» here, although the context concerns the husband's testimony.]

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿والخامِسَةُ أنَّ لَعْنَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾ — it is permissible to say "والخامِسَةَ أنَّ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ", and likewise "والخامِسَةُ أنَّ غَضَبَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها" and "اَلْخامِسَةَ", both. Whoever says "والخامِسَةَ" (accusative), it is in the sense of "وَيَشْهَدُ الخامِسَةَ" (and he testifies the fifth).
